Review Text:
Absolutely wonderful experience! The flight itself is fantastic, and we loved the sights, the employees are where this tour really shines!

We traveled with our baby son (2.5mo), and Eldridge at the check-in desk was incredible! The check-in and safety orientation process was incredibly easy, and Eldridge was very patient as my wife needed to step away to feed our son ahead of the flight.

We were joined by another young family with a more mobile older child, and both Eldridge and the pilot, Kamaka, were hyper aware of where she was at as well as recommending someone hold her hand as another plane was coming in while we all loaded into our plane to ensure her safety.

As for the flight itself, Kamaka was an amazing pilot and guid! They take passenger weights and plane balancing seriously, and they also do what they can to keep groups together. We were fortunate to have a beautiful day for sightseeing, and Kamaka even helped us spot a pod of dolphins as well as a couple different whales breaching.

For young families, this is the tour to do, and while we brought our little guy his own hearing protection, it sounded like they had some available as well.

We were debating between a plane and helicopter, and ended up going with the plane due to general safety considerations. We were a bit worried about the view from the plane vs a helicopter, but the windows on the plane were great, and Kamaka did a great job ensuring everyone had an equal opportunity for viewing everything.

10/10 would do again in a heartbeat when we’re back (hopefully soon!), and this will be our top recommendation to family and friends visiting Kauai going forward!

Thank you Eldridge and Kamaka!!

We opted for the airplane over the helicopter, as the plane was more economical and a safer option to see Kauai. A video of your flight can be purchased for $50 and is a great way to remember your time in paradise. Our experience booking through TripAdvisor was seamless and easy. The cancellation policy made it easy for a change of plans outside the 24 hour cancellation window. If traveling to Kauai, I recommend booking early. They fill up the seats on plane days in advance. Review Text: Our Wings Over Kauai Deluxe Sightseeing Flight was - without any doubt - the best and most memorable of all the excursions we did in Hawai'i.  Our pilot, Marcus, was exceptionally competent and provided interesting narration, telling us about what we were seeing.  He made sure that he flew by or around areas of particular interest so that passengers on both sides of the small plane could get the very best views.  There are no bad seats on this flight!  Everyone had a big window and a quality headset that provided clear two-way communications.  It was much quieter than a helicopter ride and apparently uses only half the fuel of a helicopter flight of similar duration.  We were so amazed by what we saw that we said "WOW!" over and over again and took soooo many photos!  After the flight we bought the video that Marcus made of our flight using footage from the cameras underneath the wings of the plane.  We are so glad we did.  The quality of the video is excellent and includes the narration that we heard on our flight.  We cannot say enough good things about Marcus and this excellent sightseeing flight!  Thank you, Marcus!

Review Title: Not to be missed experience on Kauai!
Review Text:
WOW! Just WOW! Our flight with Wings Over Kauai is one of the activities I was most looking forward to on our trip, and it totally delivered! It was truly the most magical and breathtaking experience of my life.

I know there are many options for seeing Kauai by air, including both helicopters and small airplanes, but let me convince you that Wings Over Kauai is the way to go.

1) The tour lasts about 1 hour and allows you to see more of the island that the helicopters, which usually skip the south shore on their flights.
2) There are no middle seats! This guarantees that everyone on the plane will get a window seat, and if the plane isn't at full capacity (our plane was max 6 passengers), then everyone is seated on the right which is the best view on the tour.
3) The cost is about half the cost of the helicopters. Let me repeat that, it costs about half of what the helicopters charge!
4) They have GoPro cameras attached to each wing and one inside the plane which record the flight. You can purchase an edited video of your actual flight which is 100% worth it IMO!
5) Our pilot was Marcus and he was absolutely fantastic! He is a birder, like my sister, and before our flight he even wrote down tips on where to see birds on the island. He did an incredible job narrating throughout our flight, and the flight itself was incredibly smooth and comfortable. Marcus truly went above and beyond and made our experience even better than I could have imagined.
6) If you are prone to motion sickness, often times the small planes can provide a smoother flight with less rapid changes in motion than helicopters.
7) I actually prefer that the plane flies a bit higher and provides a better panorama and wider shots than helicopters that fly closer to the terrain. If you have a camera with a good zoom lens, you can still get really nice close up shots!
8) Did I mention it's about half the price of the helicopters?

Review Title: Best way to see Kauai's beauty!
Review Text:
Full disclosure- I suffer from motion sickness fairly easily. I've tried boat rides on calm waters, which end badly for me, so I knew touring the Na Pali coast via raft or helicopter were not options. After extensive researching, I finally decided to try Wings Over Kauai. They advertised their Airvan plane as like riding a bus. This would probably be the best/only option for seeing a glimpse Kauai's awesome landscape.

Booking the trip was very easy. The price per couple was totally reasonable. Checking in for the flight was also easy. Val checked us in and took us into the back room where she went over the safety briefing and let us know what to expect on the tour. Marcus, our pilot, as also in the office checking the weather conditions.

After our final weigh in- we went to the tarmac where Val took a couple pictures of the groups in front of the plane. We donned our life jacket pouches and head sets and waited for take off.

Our pilot, Marcus, was amazing. Super friendly and knowledgeable about the island. He also was a great DJ, queuing up music appropriate for what we were seeing (Jurassic Park Theme when flying over the Jurassic Park waterfall). The views are breathtaking. Our Airvan plane had huge windows so nothing was ever obstructed. The entire flight was a little over an hour and did a tour of pretty much the entire island.

Unfortunately I did end up getting sick towards the end of the tour, though it was entirely my fault. The plane ride itself was smooth, except for the small bump here and there. Val warned us motion sickness sufferers to not take too many pictures out of the window. I did not follow this advice- the beauty was too tempting! Thankfully on board they supply a small cooler filled with ginger candies and water. I would definitely still do this tour over again and will have no problem recommending this activity for other Kauai visitors!

Review Text:
My partner booked this flight tour as he originally wanted a flight with an instructor (he’s a qualified pilot) but these were fully booked. This turned out to work in our favour as it meant that he got to see so much more without having to concentrate on flying.
Our pilot was Bruce and he was an excellent tour guide in the four-seater Cessna. He was funny and warm and pointed out loads of interesting sights, including a shoal of fish in a bay, and various movie locations. When I mentioned that I liked Jurassic Park he made a point of showing us filming locations and even played the soundtrack at one point, which made us laugh. He’s also a very interesting person, and we enjoyed chatting with him throughout our flight.
I was worried that I would maybe get travel sick on the flight as I sometimes do when my partner’s flying but I was absolutely fine, thanks to flying in the morning when it was cooler. Snacks and drinks were provided but neither of us had any as we were so engrossed in the tour.
We were lucky with perfect blue skies and calm conditions and I actually felt like staying on the plane and doing the tour all over again, it was that good!
This really was a highlight of our trip, and we’d highly recommend it.

Review Title: Nice Trips by Wings Over Kauai
Review Text:
At last week of December 2018, we visited Kauai. We planned to view Kauai from sky during our trip. So, we booked “Wings Over Kauai” air plane trip. One of the purpose to select air trip is to view Na Pali coast of Kauai easily, which can be reached by two days trekking or by availing boat. We select Wings Over Kauai air plane trip instead of helicopter. Because, as far my idea goes, helicopter fly closely to the objects like hills and waterfalls. But, in this manner over all view will not available. Another important reason was in helicopter trip window seat is not guaranteed. Almost 50% of passenger will not get window seat. In my idea view will be much restricted if window seat is not available. But, air plane which is used by Wings Over Kauai is a six seaters plane and every seat have a big window.
We booked our trip on December 27, 2018. They prefer that customer should arrive half an hour before start time of flight. Though we were arrived in time other group of our flight became late due to traffic jam on road. But, the company wait for those tourist until they arrived, delaying departure of the flight (Though flight can be departed without those customers, and there was no chance of any loss of the company). It indicates they also care for their customers and not only the money.
Pilot of that flight was Mr. Bruce who was a very nice person and guided us very nicely throughout our tour. Weather was clear and our views from the aircraft was excellent. Mr. Bruce inform us continuously about the location over where the air crafts were flying. We enjoyed that tour very much. We noticed one thing that views are better from the windows other side of pilot seat. Due to orientation of the route followed by the air plane. Though sometimes Mr. Bruce rotate the air plane such that everyone could get the best views. Time of the flight was about one hour. We enjoyed our tour very much. If we plan to visit Kauai, we will avail this tour again.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: This is how you should see Kauai
Review Text: What a wonderful way to see the island! We took the private 2-person tour on the Cessna and were treated like family. Capt. Bruce (he’s also Dr. Bruce, a retired research scientist!) and Val were very professional and took good care of us. We were unsure of this morning’s trip as the weather forecast was not looking good. Rain and clouds were about to roll in when we got to the airport. Val greeted us cheerfully, checked us in and went through the safety briefing with us thoroughly. I immediately knew that they took safety seriously. We then waited as we were early for our scheduled departure. It started to rain shortly thereafter and Bruce then called us into the office and showed us the big rain clouds over the Lihue & Hanalei area on the computer. He was very honest and told us that we will likely not have clear views over some areas. So he gave us a choice to reschedule, a refund or to go ahead with the tour (assuring us it was safe to do so). What an honest and professional business! We decided to go ahead and was prepared for a less than stellar experience. Boy, were we wrong! While it was cloudy, the sights were still wonderful as Bruce expertly navigated through the clouds and showed us the spectacular Na Pali Coast and the breathtaking Waimea Canyon. We had to turn around at Hanalei due to the storm clouds (again safety first!) while some other operators decided to go through the area. I knew this as I could hear all the chatter over the radio. A couple others did turn around and followed Bruce’s lead. He must be well respected by the flying community! We made it back to Lihue airport safely with full of wonderful memories. Thank you Bruce for your wonderful sense of humor and knowledge about the island. I enjoyed being your “co-pilot”!

Review Text: We booked this tour after our catamaran trip was cancelled due to rough seas (we are here late October), and I am an extremely nervous flyer.  Let me tell you, firstly, the service was excellent.  The staff really cared that I was nervous and took every opportunity to make me comfortable, I so appreciated that.  As soon as we took off however - I had forgotten my nerves.  Holy wow.... Kaua'i, what a treasure.  Marcus was our guide, he was very knowledgeable and made us feel at home and comfortable straight away.  For those wanting to take images of Na Pali- I recommend you book the private tour - either on the cessna, or book out the entire air-van.  I can imagine if I was seated on the opposite side of the air-van, I wouldn't have had the unforgettable experience I had - we were lucky that the others booked in our tour did not show, and we had the air-van to ourselves.  From the beginning of the flight to the end, the scenery was like another world.  From lush green, untouched growth and waterfalls to the stunning Waimea Canyon, to the 5000ft vertical peaks of Na Pali and inner Kaua'i landscape beyond, it is truly a life changing experience to see.   When we landed, I wanted to get back in and do it again, and to top it all off, our amazing pilot played music from Skyrim when we entered the Na Pali area - LIFE MADE!  Don't hesitate, just book in!!!

Review Title: Beautiful way to see the island
Review Text:
Plane vs. Helicopter seems to be a matter of thrill vs. camera shots. In the plane, it seems you can get better camera shots because you are further away from everything, but we saw helicopters underneath us who could go quite close to the waterfalls and craters, etc. I imagine it would be awesome to experience but even more difficult to capture. If money were no issue, I might opt for the helicopter but I have no regrets on our plane experience.
My friend and I booked the slightly larger plane because we wanted the bubble windows for better visibility. Unfortunately because there were not four of us, they called us to switch to the private jet, which I was a bit bummed about due to less window visibility (which they at least admitted) even though they didn't charge extra. Regardless, views were nicer on the side than I was worried we'd get (if you're short, it is hard to see out the front even as co-pilot). Doug was super calm and very friendly, which helps if you get altitude sickness (so do their ginger candies and water). Getting there 30min early seemed unnecessary since they didn't see us til 10 min before, yet again were very friendly. Overall would highly recommend seeing Kauai by air, whatever way it is that best works for you and your schedule/budget.

Review Title: Private Cessna is the only way to fly!
Review Text:
We decided to splurge during our visit to Kauai and booked a private flight on Wings Over Kauai's Cessna 172. It was a bit more expensive than the group flight on the Caravan, but so worth it. Imagine having your own private chauffeured hour to fly around the island!

We were warmly welcomed to the flightline by Val. She took our information and gave us a quick rundown of what to expect during our flight. She also discreetly weighed us
to ensure the weight and balance is set up properly for the flight.

We met Captain Bruce and after introductions were made all around, we all walked out to the plane. So much nicer than boarding a commercial flight. Yeah, the plane was smaller but no one was fighting you for overhead bin space! As an #AvGeek (read "plane nerd!") I called shotgun and my wife was nice enough to indulge me. Bruce also teaches flying, so he took the time to explain flight dynamics and how the airplane respond to different inputs. We both worked the pre-flight takeoff list and after waiting for a Hawaiian Airlines 717 to land and vacate the runway, we were off.

It was a beautiful day for flying. Puffy white clouds dotted the sky and visibility was forever. Mt. Waiʻaleʻale was almost totally visible, which is vary rare! Bruce kept up a running commentary was we overflew Poipu Beach, the Waimea Canyon, the Napali Coast, then across Hanalei Bay and back down towards Lihue. When we were halfway through our flight, my wife commenced the drink service with bottles and cans from the cooler under the back seat!

We were thrilled with our choice of Wings Over Kauai. We highly recommend the private Cessna flight for a group of 2 or 3 people. Even if you take the group flight on the Caravan, seeing the island from the air is a fantastic trip and should be considered a "Must Do!" during your visit to the Kauai.

Review Title: One of the greatest excursions I've ever done!!
Review Text:
One of the greatest excursions I've ever done and probably will ever do! We were visiting Kauai for a few days after Maui, and booked the sightseeing flight tour with Wings Over Kauai as our first stop after we arrived at the airport. I highly recommend planning this as the first thing you do on Kauai, because you get a birds eye view of the entire island before you start exploring it by land. It was truly fascinating to see how diverse the different regions of the island are; lush forests/waterfalls, beautiful coastline beaches & mountainous cliffs.

This is a family run business and they went above and beyond to take such good care of us. Mary and Captain Bruce were some of the kindest people we've ever met, truly care about their customer's experience, and made it clear why they love the island so much. They were extremely knowledgeable about Kauai, both local recommendations and about its rich history.

I was initially a little anxious about flying in a small plane, but felt extremely safe and comfortable with Captain Bruce and the smooth ride from take off to landing. Review Text:

After reading the great views for Wings Over Kauai, I decided to give the small plane tour a try. Not sure I'll ever do another helicopter tour again, if there is a small plane option.

We opted for the Cessna, and it was just me, my wife and the pilot. Bruce was our pilot and he was fantastic! Great commentary along the way, and his experience flying this tour showed as he charted a perfect path around the island.

The flight seemed so much smoother than the helicopters. And my original concerns about just flying past sights without the ability to hover were unfounded.

Not sure if it is always the case, but when they say 65 minute tour they mean it. Pretty sure we were in the air for the full 65 minutes, though it went by way too fast. No discounting for taxi time, etc. or rounding an hour down to 50 minutes.

At the end of the flight they provided us with a list of Bruce's favorites. Wish we had that at the beginning of our visit as his recommendations were spot-on.

Review Text:
I have a slightly different perspective - I flew with both Bruce and Marcus as part of my ongoing training as a private pilot. They were both fantastic instructors AND fantastic tour guides. I also flew 3 times over three weeks, and during the last 2 flights I also brought my girls (one at a time - only one passenger at a time in the Cessna 172. A bunch of folks can fly in the Airvans). My girls had a GREAT time and I got to be the "pilot" even though I was the student.
Maybe the other tours have great guides, but I have a hard time believing they are better guides than Bruce and Marcus. Bruce has lived on the Island for nearly 30 years, and knows the geology, history, ecology - the best beaches and most importantly, the flying!
Both Marcus and Bruce provided great instruction on situational awareness, the winds aloft and terrain effects, and how to keep passengers calm and enjoying the flight. If you are not an aviator, let me say this - these guys are safety minded, vigilant, experienced, and exercise great flight discipline. I learned a TON flying with them.
THE TOUR: beyond beautiful! On every one of my 3 flights we saw new things, from barking sands, to the Na Pali, to the interior of the island, to the biggest resorts. My girls had an amazing time. I recommend doing this early on in your time on the island, as it gave me a mental map of how varied the terrain was, and quickly formed a list of things to see and do. I can also say that you could even do it twice or more, as a passenger, and get new things every time.
If you are an experienced pilot, or just learning like me, you have to do this! If you already have your PPL, fly right seat, as the flights rotate around the island from south east to northwest (na pali) and you will see much more. I stayed in left seat as I wanted to be consistent with the controls for the time being. Having the freedom to fly on vacation was something new to me, and I plan on doing it in norway, out in Colorado, Florida, etc. It will be hard to top the beauty of this trip - one of the best things I've ever done on vacation. Bruce, Ellen, and Marcus run a great experience. 5/5!

Review Title: No luck getting into the air, but Wings is still the best!
Review Text:
My husband and I were rained or otherwise "bad-weathered" out of every adventure we planned on Kauai. Couldn't hike Kalalau due to the river crossing being flooded.
Couldn't kayak or sail the coast due to 24 ft swells. Never got to fly in the Cessna with Doug due to high winds the first day, and low cloud cover and/or rain the other three times we tried. Luckily, we had booked our flight through Wings over Kauai, and originally booked it for our first full day on the island, which ended up giving us the most shots on goal in terms of chances to reschedule and hopefully get up there. Each time we arrived, Doug walked us through the weather, visibility, turbulence, and gave us the choice of getting up there with the limited visibility/bumpy ride or reschedule. We rescheduled three times, and while it never worked out, we still appreciated the customer service and flexible policies of Wings. Our last chance was the AM before our flight off island, and when it became clear the weather still wasn't going to cooperate, we were promptly issued a refund. One thing both my husband and I noticed was that every time we went to the terminal to try to get into the air, the helicopter tours were still going out. So, my guess is they have a limited refund policy and therefore people opt to take the flight even if you don't see anything and/or it's potentially dangerous. Doug and the rest of Wings were incredibly helpful, friendly, and clearly interested in making sure everyone gets the best and safest experience flying over Kauai. I can't wait to go back to Kauai again to accomplish all the adventures we were denied our first time out, and we will definitely be re-booking our tour with Wings over Kauai! We've already passed on their info to three other people we know are heading to Kauai in the next few months. It's so rare to encounter such amazing customer service in this day and age. We can honestly say Wings was a highlight of our time in Kauai even though we didn't even get to fly!

Review Text:

We began planning our excursions for this vacation several months ago and decided to use independent third party operators in lieu of the expensive ones offered through the cruise line. Professionalism: Upon arriving in Kauai on 4/15, I decided to call Wings Over Kauai to see if they have any cancellations. Using the local number, I did not reach them on the first try and figured I was out of luck. Immediately after hanging up, I received a call from Ellen, she was very friendly and said they had some openings to accommodate one passenger and I booked a flight on their 8 seater for 11am. I received email confirmation within minutes ... outstanding customer service and I was a happy camper.

Performance: I read many of the Trip Advisor comments and let me tell you they do what is advertised, and more! Ellen picked me up at precisely the right time and shuttled me from the ABC Store to the air terminal. Her daughter Mary took care of the reservation paperwork along wth weigh-in to make sure they balance out the seating. Mary said Marcus was our pilot and he would be arriving shortly, and sure enough, he was just landing from a previous flight. Mary and Marcus escorted the 4 of us to the plane, photos were taken by Mary as a souvenir and she said she'd email them after the flight. I felt like the lucky one with the co-pilot seat (Marcus probably didn't feel as lucky)...guess they needed to put me up there for proper weight distribution. Views were absolutely incredible -- from take off to landing, and it was great to fly over the harbor and see the cruise ship at the pier. Marcus' narration of the landmarks, simply outstanding and his piloting skills phenomenal! Very little turbulence, partly cloudy skies and a very smooth flight allowed for some spectacular photograph. The beautiful island music playing through the headsets was a great touch!

Pride: Upon landing we were greeted by Mary and she helped Marcus with getting us off the plane. Bottled water or ginger ale was offered and it sure was appreciated. Marcus asked us to come inside because he had a parting gift for us. Each of us was presented a CD with the Hawaiian music played on our flight and a color picture that was taken at the beginning of the flight as the jewel case cover. It was no charge! A simple gesture that goes a long way in my book, and the kind of thing that will bring me back to them the next time I visit Kauai.

Price: I highly recommend Wings Over Kauai should you want to take advantage of the spectacular Pali Coast scenery not viewable by land. Their price is cheaper than several others I checked out, so please call the (808) local number to discuss your adventure of a lifetime.

I have taken many, many excursions through various cruise lines and bar none, this was the best ever in my opinion. Many thanks to Ellen, Mary and Marcus - and Mary, thank you for bringing me all the way back to the terminal.

Review Title: A brilliant way to see the Kauai
Review Text:
While we were on vacation in Kauai we wanted to see as much of the island as possible and, as I’m a pilot, looked for an opportunity to fly and sight-see from a fixed wing aircraft. Helicopters are ok but they can be a bit of a nuisance for people on the ground. Plus Bruce’s Cessna 172 is a much less expensive way to do this. We arranged (before we left home in North Carolina) to take an island tour via dual flight instruction from Bruce Coulombe of Wings Over Kauai. We met Bruce’s colleague at Lihue airport and she did a short briefing and the weight and balance. Bruce then showed us around the aircraft and we climbed aboard. After a thoroughly professional preflight and engine start/run up we were ready to go. My wife was in the back and I had the right seat – for a better view of the island. We were cleared for take off from runway 3 and immediately after lift-off could see the beautiful island spread out below, and as it happened the resort where we were staying. We flew along the coast and Bruce – who has lived on the island for a long time, initially while working as a scientist for a big agriculture company and then for the next few thousand hours of flying around Kauai – pointed out the places we were flying over. Basically for the next 50 minutes this included all of the island highlights, and Bruce’s comments and background information made this a data-rich tour. When we were approaching Lihue airport, we had to do a 360 because of departing traffic, and then were cleared to land on runway 3.
This was a brilliant way for us to see the island, as well as for me to get 1.1 hours unforgettable instruction for the logbook. The helicopter tours may be ok for passengers, but believe us, Bruce’s tour will stay with you – a pilot – as one of the best flights ever, and especially if you get the dvd of the flight for an accurate record with all the details. And with money you save flying with Bruce rather than doing a helicopter tour, you could have dinner for the next 3 nights at the Bamboo Grill and Sushi overlooking the bay at Lihue. What a great day!
Aloha and mahalo Bruce.

Review Text: Sandy & I signed up for the flight with Bruce Coulombe, owner of "Wings Over Kauai". Bruce has over 7,000 flights touring Kauai since 1994. The weather was beautiful and with Bruce's expert advice I navigated and flew while sightseeing. Sandy took excellent photos from the rear seat behind me. I own a '70 V35B Bonanza and Bruce was excellent with his power setting suggestions, airspeed and altitude directions all the way to a right seat landing. This is an excellent experience for any pilot from a high time retired Airline pilot, like myself to a novice thinking about taking up flying. Well Done. Thanks Bruce, Ellen, Carter and Mary, a true Family operation! Marty Noonan

Review Title: Great option for an aerial overview-Affordable and Great Service
Review Text:
We were looking at Helicopter tours, but I read so many great reviews for Wings Over Kauai, that I preferred the plane. My husband wanted to do a doors off helicopter but there were weight limits and the potential of being crammed in a middle seat. I didn't want to pay a lot and be stuck in the middle. My husband, friend, and I decided to try this option.

We did the airvan tour. Booking and check-in were smooth. There was plenty of parking near the office. The plane also had plenty of room. We went with one other nice couple. Customer service was excellent. The flights were pretty full but they squeezed us in for a 4:00 p.m. flight and it was perfect. The sun was out and the lighting was great for pictures. Bruce personalized the tour and gave us a good background of the island too. They also had drinks in the plane if anyone wanted them.
After the flight, they gave us a CD with music and our pictures in front of the plane at no extra charge, which was a nice gesture.

I also think you got more minutes in the air with the plane and less rocky motion so if anyone is subject to motion sickness, this would be a smoother ride and nice way to see the island.
In sum, we highly recommend this as it is a great value for an aerial tour and excellent customer service.

Review Title: A Must For Your Kauai Visit!
Review Text: I was originally looking into helicopter tours but was worried about my wife getting motion sickness and the costs are pretty expensive.  When I found Wings Over Kauai on a TripAdvisor search and saw the other positive reviews it seemed like the perfect solution for our visit.  I booked the private 2-person Cessna tour and it was half of what a helicopter tour that wasn't even private was going to cost.  Our experience with booking, confirmation, directions and everything leading up to the flight was flawless.  On the day of our flight we met with Bruce who owns the company and was also our pilot and went through a thorough pre-flight briefing and were on our way.  Bruce shared his vast knowledge of the island as we flew by all the spectacular sights which added a nice touch to the tour.  We started out at 3:30 in hopes that the weather would be a little clearer (always a gamble on any day) and the sun would be better for some pictures along the Waimea Canyon and Na Pali Coast.  We lucked out and the scenery was amazing.  While you aren't right up on things like you might be in a helicopter I found that the views were still excellent and met my expectations.  Although the configuration of an airplane isn't the optimum for taking professional photos (and really only a doors off helicopter is optimal), my wife and I managed to get many great shots.  Wings Over Kauai also provides the option to purchase a high def go-pro video of your flight which is a nice touch as well that you could also grab still images from.  Overall our experience was excellent and I would highly recommend Bruce and Wings Over Kauai as an alternative to high priced and crowded heli-tours.

Review Text: We booked the air and sea combo tour with Blue Dolphin Charters and Wings over Kauai -- both were a great value. We ended up rebooking for the day we also had our boat tour -- not the best idea since you're driving from one part of the island to the other, but still doable.  We caught Bruce's last flight of the day at 4PM and were lucky to have the whole flight to ourselves. Bruce is very knowledgeable about the island and we were able to see incredible views. Part of the perks of doing the plane over the helicopter would definitely be the pricing  -- it's almost half as much. Though a helicopter is better able to get you down into those tighter areas, such as Waimea Canyon, we still had plenty of great views and picture ops. They were also quite alright with me using my gopro to record a chunk of the flight. Bruce provided complimentary drinks while we were up in the air and a nice, added bonus -- they took our picture in front of the plane and printed the pic out on the jacket of a DVD highlighting the views we saw during the flight (at no extra cost). It's a nice little touch to have a pic of us before our flight and a little highlight video. Thanks, Bruce and your team. Would definitely recommend!

Review Title: Smooth Ride Over Beautiful Kauai Island
Review Text: We had booked the Airvan for a private charter. The debate of helicopter vs airplane was a big deal with the five of us. What I really liked about the airplane is that the whole family can fly at the same time and able to talk with one another. The other concern I had if my stomach can handle the helicopter's maneuvers. There were a helicopter every 10 min. over our heads when we were at every beach and hikes, kind of sad. There were five in our group and four sat on the right side. I got to sit in the back next to my daughter-in-law, kind of in the middle. I stretched to see and Marcus turned for me to see specific areas of the Napili Coast. Prior to the flight, the young lady at the office kept bringing up that they might not fly due to the weather. I wanted to wait until Marcus came back from the flight to see how it goes first. Marcus passed out a couple of DVDs to the previous group while they were thanking him. Review Text:
We chose Wings Over Kauai as my boyfriend had never been on a small plane, and it was MUCH cheaper than the helicopter tours (our tour was $300). This company had the best customer service ever! On our scheduled day, we arrived early and Mary got us checked in, weighed, etc. The wind was really picking up and it looked like a big rainstorm was moving in. Mary checked with Marcus (the pilot) to see how conditions were elsewhere on the island. Marcus replied that conditions were not very good for sightseeing and getting worse. He and Mary suggested that we should cancel for the day and try again the next morning, in the hopes of a much better trip. Note: we had booked an afternoon trip but Marcus and Mary said that morning trips are usually a better bet for good weather and visibility. We got booked onto a tour the next morning with no problem and at no charge.
Meanwhile, we asked Mary for recommendations on what to do since it looked like a thunderstorm was moving in. She suggested going to the west or south side of the island which she said was usually sunny. Since we had a Jeep, she recommended we go to Polihale Beach. This turned out to be breathtaking, and we were so glad she recommended it!
The next morning we went on our tour. There were two other people with us, and we all had window seats. Also provided in the plane were waters, cool wet towels, ginger candies, and ginger ale for motion sickness. My boyfriend got motion sick, and the pilot and other passengers were most helpful in helping me get him the towels, ginger, etc. to feel better.
Marcus was an excellent guide, and had personal stories about some of the sights we saw, as well as general information, which helped make the flight tour that much better.
We had our picture taken with the plane before flight, and when we returned, we got a CD with our picture and some of the music that was played during the flight. Unlike some other companies, there was no charge for this great souvenir.
We thought the plane tour was better than doing a helicopter tour as we were able to fly higher and get better views and pictures of sights such as the Na Pali coast. We saw helicopters that were flying lower and closer to the cliffs, but we preferred to have our views of the entire cliff from top to bottom, instead of just a small portion of the cliffs.
This was our favorite thing we did on Kauai, this is a must-do!

Review Title: Spectacular Views Delivered by this Family-Run Business
Review Text: Wings Over Kauai was one of the first tours we booked when planning for our stay on Kauai January 29, 2015. We walked a short distance from where our ship (Pride of America) was anchored to meet up with Mary from WOK. She drove us to the Lihue Airport where we met her brother, Carter. Review Text:
As a pilot with a student certificate, I wanted to take the controls myself and Wings over Kauai was the obvious choice. We booked an instructional flight in the 172 with Bruce, the owner of the company. Now, for all certified pilots out there: you will not be able to rent a plane by yourself in Kauai and neither should you. The tour traffic (especially helicopters) is busy, constant and organized. It is important to check in on the advisory frequency for position updates and if you don't know the informal landmarks, you'll be spending your flight trying to figure out which valley a chopper is going to pop out out of next. Additionally, you have to deal with mountain/ocean flying, comply with noise abatement rules and the Pacific Missile Range restricted area. Let Bruce handle the radio and big picture navigation so you can enjoy the flying and scenery.

Since my flight was pre-checkride, Bruce threw in a few exam questions here and there, gave me general directions, offered some helpful tips that you can only get from an 11,000 hour pilot, and otherwise let me pick my path between the clouds. He pointed out landmarks and places of interest, and supplied some tour-guide type narration.

We had a good weather day (there are always some clouds in Kauai) and the view was spectacular. We followed the established clockwise direction around the island which is flown by all tour aircraft. We saw whales, the steep cliffs of the Na'pali Coast, craters, beaches, reefs etc.

The main difference to a helicopter tour (which we did the same day) is that helicopters can get into spaces the plane cannot. The two are different experiences. With the helo rides you're part of a group and get herded like cattle through the safety video and the tour. With the plane, you miss out on those tight canyons and close-up waterfalls, but you have your own plane and can pick your route. Plus, it's a lot cheaper AND YOU GET TO FLY YOURSELF. If you load the plane with 3 people the price is about $100 per person/hour. Compare that to $260/person on the choppy for the 55 min ride. Plus, if you're stuck in the back middle seats on the helo, your visibility is quite restricted. On the Cessna the windows might be smaller, but at least everyone has their own.

Anyway, we returned to Lihue Airport, I made a nice-enough landing, and taxied back to the ramp in front of two Hawaiian Airlines Boeings. If you're a pilot, you know what I'm talking about.

All in all, Wings over Kauai is a down-to-earth, family-run small business, and not a multi-island, slick and smooth helo operation. No memorabilia shop, t-shirts and upsells. They have GoPros mounted on the plane for those who like that sort of thing, but they don't push their video as much as the other outfits. Wings over Kauai is a more than viable alternative to the helicopter rides, especially if you don't want to spend $750 for a family of three. They also have a Cessna Caravan for larger groups (or mixed groups).

Review Text:
We really had a great time with Wings Over Kauai. We were in the area for a day and a half on the Pride Of America cruise ship. I decided to schedule our flight for 930am the second day. The first day we arrived it was pretty cloudy and rainy, so I was bummed that the weather was going to stay the same and we wouldn't see much. Thankfully the second day it was totally clear and nice! Even the top of Waialeale was clear!

The day of our trip we were picked up promptly near the cruise ship as arraigned. We went over the basics- safety, weigh-in, and some pictures next to the plane. Our pilot was Josh (a former American Airlines pilot), and he got us buckled in to our assigned seats. I was in the copilot seat, and my wife was behind me. Once in the air, Josh told us lots of facts about what we were seeing while music played. The Na Pali coast was beautiful and we had great viewing weather. I did get a bit of haze in my pictures, which looked worse on the camera's LCD than the final picture (I used a telephoto lens with a polarizing filter). Before we knew it, it was time to land. I really enjoyed getting to listen to air traffic control the whole time also.

Once back at the airport, they gave everyone a free gift (I won't ruin the surprise). They also offered to sell us a DVD of the full flight, filmed by GoPros mounted under the wings and inside the cabin. The price was very reasonable, and it arrived by the time we got home. It was a great keepsake to have, and the views were so much better than what I captured on my camera. They offered to drop us off back at the cruise ship or the mall, and gave my wife a flower for her hair. Everyone we met was extremely nice and we really enjoyed the flight.

One note, if you have even the slightest problem with motion sickness, take a dramamine pill before you fly. We were lucky to have a pretty smooth flight, but small slow planes like this are more prone to thermals and winds than large jets. We experienced a few quick stomach-drops, that felt kind of a like a roller coaster hill. My wife did feel a little airsick, but the dramamine stopped her from throwing up. They do have a cooler on board with sprite and ginger chews, but better safe than sorry.

Don't hesitate to get a great view of Kauai, book a flight!

Review Title: Fantastic tour!!  A must for Kauai!
Review Text: We went in their small plane for the tour over Kauai, there were six of us including the pilot.  They picked us up at the ABC store, just up the street from the pier, where our ship docked.  If you don't want to take the ten minute walk you can jump on the free shuttle that takes you to the little mall where the ABC store located.  When I read all the previous comments about Wings Over Kauai we decided to go with them, and we're very happy we did!!  For $125.00 US we got a whole hour in the air.  If they keep that up they will continue to be busy and recommended by people like myself.  I've already told many people to go with them.  They were nice enough to offer us free water and pop during our flight, that was great!  The best part of the tour, is seeing Kauai, it's beautiful!!  For anyone sitting on the passenger side of the plane, you will see better.  If your on the pilots side, you will see everything but not as well and throughly as the others, but the pilot does try his best.  I think it's due to the time it takes to fly the plane around so everyone can see as well.  I would still recommend it anyways.  If price doesn't matter and you want a shorter ride then you can take a helicopter ride, which flies lower and takes you closer to the mountains.  Make sure to bring your camera!!  Go to the washroom and get in the plane!!  They do have good walk up steps to the plane, so even if you have some disabilities you shouldn't have a problem.  If you leave yourself three hours from getting to the mall, filling out the paperwork, getting weighed, get on the plane and the flight back, you should be good.  Ellen picked us up and was,so nice.  We met her husband and our pilot, Josh, along with Ellen's daughter, and they were all so nice and friendly.  Josh was an excellent,pilot, constantly talking to us all during the flight and answering any questions we had.  Can't lose taking this tour, especially as its the only way to see the canyon and the Na Pali coast without hiking and a boat, which would take days.  Kauai is so beautiful and you appreciate it more from the air.

Review Text:
Kauai is our favorite island. There’s just something different about it. It has a different feel, a different vibe. Maybe it’s the chickens everywhere, or the cattle or the more mature landscape. Just not sure. From the air, it’s gorgeous. We flew Wings Over Kauai. Very, very nice people. We were very lucky in that the other people on our flight cancelled, so we had the entire Caravan to ourselves. Bruce, the owner, was our pilot. We took off on 30, NW, turned right and circled the island clockwise. Got great pictures during a flyover of the Crown at dock. The day was partly cloudy with clouds and rain over the center of the island. The water was pure aqua blue, the coastline just picture perfect rocks and white spray and the green of the trees contrasting with the red of the soil could not be done justice in a photo. We cut inland up Wameia Canyon, saw the Jurassic Park waterfall, flew inland of the Pacific Missile Test Range main base, but cut back out over the ocean just before we go to the northern most telemetry radars sitting on top of one giant cliff.

Flew along the Napoli Coast. Saw the trail wind its way through the cliffs, on top of huge sea caves and along knife edge ridges of rock. Broke back over the northern coast over the resorts and golf courses and the locations they filmed Jurassic World. Cut around the NW part of the island, flew a circle around the Fantasy Island waterfall, saw the cattle grazing in almost chartreuse meadows, flew back over the ship and landed back on runway 30. The whole trip was about 70 minutes, at a ground speed of around 90mph. Judy filmed the whole thing with the action cam, and I took about 160+ stills. We also ordered a video of the flight. They had GoPro’s on each wing.

This was one of the best value excursions we’ve ever had in Hawaii. Judy did get a little queasy coming around the hills to the NW of the airport. The air was a bit bumpy, but not bad at all. Nothing like the helicopter we took in Juneau in 2001.

The day we were flying out of Kauai to go back home.

He informed us that there was a very minor mechanical problem with the plane and he couldn't take us up. He wasn't able to get a mechanic in to do a repair that day. Marcus and the owners wife went into the office.I figured a refund was coming. While talking with my wife,they came out and went over to Air Adventures who are in the same building. Air Adventures came over and offered to take us up, but not until 4:30.Their pilot was already doing the last trip of the day.Great I said. Review Title: Awesome Air Tour of Kauai - especially if value keeping your lunch down
Review Text:
So this was my 3rd time to Hawaii, 2nd with my family. I vividly remember my first time, which was my honeymoon, because that's when I had my first helicopter ride in Hawaii. I spent a small fortune on a "champagne" tour and ended up losing my lunch because helicopters can be very disorienting in tight spaces like waterfalls and canyons.

So this time I took a different strategy and booked a 60 minute flight with Wings Over Kauai. And I must say the experience was very enjoyable and didn't bother my stomach in the least.

Bruce, the Pilot, was very friendly and personable. He is also one of the owners of the company and turned his flying hobby into a 2nd career after leaving the agricultural field where he had a PhD.

We were a family of four and everyone had a clear window seat. We toured the entire island, including the Waimea canyon, Napali coast, and saw a half dozen great waterfalls, including the one from Fantasy Island. Sitting in the front for takeoff and landing was also pretty cool.

One thing I did not do was read the FAQ on the site about best times to fly. One suggestion was that afternoon flights gave you better lighting on the Napali coast and the canyon for photography. And while I agree that might have reduced the glare from the cockpit somewhat for photos, overall our 930am flight was fine and the weather was beautiful and my photos turned out fine. Bruce had a lot of good tips.

After the flight Bruce also provided us with some tips on his favorite things to do / places to eat which were very good.

Thanks again to Bruce and his assistant Angel for a truly great experience. I definitely felt less queazy and safer in a plane than I did in a helicopter.

Review Title: Worth the time and money if your time in Kauai is limited (cruise)
Review Text:
If on a cruise - book on your own. This is a family-owned operation with only two airplanes - Dr. Bruce Coulombe, young retired research scientist, head of the family. My wife searched Kauai flights after we booked a cruise from Tahiti to Los Angeles with stops at four Hawaiian islands. The cruise excursions are costly. Our time on Kauai was limited. Wings Over Kauai had the best price offer, and were friendly when the reservations were made (about three months in advance). Bruce met my wife and me at the cruise port and drove us to the airport. Since more people booked for the same hour, instead of flying in the larger six passenger aircraft, we volunteered to be flown in the Cessna Skyhawk - just the pilot, my wife and myself. The pilot was well versed on what we to see below. Bruce returned us to our ship.

A retired judicial professional couple who were with us on the cruise and lived on Kauai told us that the fixed wing aircraft were much safer than helicopter flights. They told us that far more helicopter accidents (fatal) occur than happens with fixed wing aircraft. Helicopters do fly closer to the canyons and water falls. Might be the reason they crash more often.

Worth the time and money spent.

The C172 he flies is in excellent condition; fuel injected, steam gauges, well maintained. I particularly liked that Bruce didn't mind me doing my own preflight or questioning him on the oil level and fuel before engine start. I really respect that.

As an instructor, Bruce is fantastic. He has input if you want it, or he'll just let you get on and fly. He's obviously a solid pilot (as he should be, at 10,000+ hours). and knows the local landscape and procedures well.

We flew around the island, safely, and enjoyably. He's got decent ANR headsets, his folks are awesome, and I can't imagine a better experience.

All in all, if you are a visiting pilot, you would be CRAZY to miss this experience. Much safer than a helicopter (not to mention cheaper), run by folks who really are focused on safety AND fun, good flight instruction (I was on the stick the whole flight). I can't say enough good things. Mahalo, Bruce!

Review Title: Wings Not Rotors Plus A 360-Degree Double Rainbow
Review Text: This is an aerial tour by plane, not by helicopter.  Another couple went with us and one of our party becomes motion sick relatively easily.  The company's FAQ's address this issue and the information was accurate.  Our pilot was aware of the issue and tried to make the ride as gentle as possible for her.  We booked the 4:00 pm Grand Deluxe Tour in the G8 AirVan.  Because the fare for two couples ($125 per person, $500.00 for the two couples) equaled the "private charter" fare, we opted for that so only the four of us and, of course, the pilot were on the plane.  Upon arrival, we were greeted by Mary who was very friendly and accommodating.  Because the weather during the day had been rainy, she did not take our credit cards until she spoke to our pilot, Josh, about the weather.  Josh had just returned from a tour and gave the green light for our flight in that his opinion was that the weather was clearing and that this would be the best tour of the day.  His prophesy was correct. The ride was relatively smooth, although there were a few bumpy spots.  However, we were fortunate to see a 360-degree double rainbow (we didn't know a 360-degree rainbow existed, but it does and can only be seen from the air) along the Napali Coast.  Simply spectacular!  The views are all from the right side of the plane.  The windows are big so it is easy to take photos if you want.  But if you just want to sit back and enjoy the experience, the plane is equipped with several cameras and you can purchase a DVD, Blue-Ray or video download link at the end of the trip ($35 for the DVD and $50 for the Blue-Ray or video download link) that shows your trip and includes the pilot's commentary, music and the passengers' conversations (you wear a headset with a mike and can talk with the other passengers and pilot).  Before the plane took off, I noticed that Mary cleaned all of the windows on the plane -- nice touch.  The plane flies at a relatively slow speed of 90 mph and the tour lasts about 65 minutes.  Josh did a nice commentary and fielded the questions we had.  Josh was friendly and according to the women in our party, "not hard to look at."  He said that he had been doing this tour for four years and had been flying in the Hawaian Islands for seven years.  If you want a great overview (no pun intended) of the island's features, including numerous waterfalls and movie locations, and  some of its attractions, we highly recommend this tour.

Review Text:
This flight was a real highlight of our trip. There were six of us, so we were able to have the six-passenger "Air-Van" all to ourselves at somewhat of a discount relative to the per person price. There were some schedule changes, but Dori in their office was very accommodating and made it work. We took the flight the first day after arriving. The areal view really oriented us to the layout of the island.

The weather was exceptional. Visibility was great, very few clouds or haze; you could see entirely across the island as well as the mountain tops. The water was flat and clear, so we could see the sand and the coral under the surface. Just after take-off we saw a whale swimming near the surface with its calf. The pilot, Captain Josh, made a 360 degree turn around this sight, so we could get a good view. We saw many other whales, but from a greater distance.

The take-offs and landings were extremely smooth, and turns were all gentle and even. If you want more of a thrill ride, you might choose the helicopters, which fly much lower and closer to the sights. We had some nervous fliers who are prone to air sickness, so the plane ride was just right for us. It was exhilarating due to the views, not the motion.

Captain Josh was friendly, knowledgeable and fun. We felt very safe and comfortable. He point out many sights, related many anecdotes and answered all our questions. We wore microphoned headsets and were all able to hear each other. Josh ran a Hawaiian and movie themed sound tract that we enjoyed very much. Since the route is primarily a clockwise circle of the island, he doubled back on a couple of occasions, so the the people on the left side of the plane would also get good views. He also navigated up canyons where both sides had good views.

The plane is equipped with about six GoPro cameras, including one wide-angle camera inside the cockpit. They construct a video with a soundtrack of the entire trip and video that includes interior and exterior views. We bought the 1080P copy of the video and are very happy we did. What a great memory!

I would happily take this same flight again.

Review Text:
We had a wonderful time on our flight with Wings Over Kauai! I had looked at helicopter tours as well, but we chose a fixed-wing flight because it's far safer (check out Kauai Underground Guide's table of helicopter tour fatalities, also because it's an awesome guide), it's half the price, and I had read reviews that the view you get from the helicopter tours is a 'luck of the draw' situation.

We booked a 4 person AirVan Private Charter, the flight takes a sort of clockwise tour of the island so we were all seated on the left to ensure we all had excellent views. And excellent views we had! Whales, canyons, Na Pali coast, waterfalls, extinct volcanoes, river valleys...you name it, we saw it, and it was stunning. The bubble windows allow you to see below and above the plane, in addition to out to the side.

Bruce, a retired agronomist and our guide to the skies, seemed almost as excited to be on our flight as we were. He proved to be an incredibly talented pilot and knowledgeable (and entertaining) guide to the Garden Isle. I love flying, but my boyfriend and sister were a bit nervous about being in a small plane--if you are, don't let this stop you from booking with Wings Over Kauai! That was probably the smoothest flight I've ever been on.

During our booking process Ellen was extremely accommodating and responsive to emails. Our original tour date wound up being incredibly stormy, and we were able to reschedule for a sunny day. Do bear in mind that Kauai is subject to changeable and sometimes stormy weather, if it is not safe to fly your tour will be cancelled. Ellen will do all she can to reschedule your tour in such an event, but if your stay is short this may be difficult. So make sure you stay for awhile, because Kauai is absolutely amazing and a Wings Over Kauai flight shouldn't be missed!!

Review Text:
If I can give them a rating of 6, I would, because they deserve it!

We did a lot of research on both the plane and helicopter tours over Kauai, and based on people's comments about safety records, customer service, and value, we finally decided on W.O.K.

They lived up to our expectations, and more. We called in to get info, and they assured us we would get a right-side seat (which gets better views). On the day of, Val did the orientation with us. She was hospitable and very courteous. Josh was our pilot and he did a great job of flying and narrating. Again the same hospitable spirit. We rode the AirVan, not the Cessna.

The plane ride itself was nothing short of spectacular. You fly higher than the helicopters, but it gave us a very good bird's eye view of the canyons and valleys, and on Kauai I think that's better then the close-up views.

Don't count on this, but a big bonus for me was, I got the co-pilot's seat, and that allowed me the perfect vantage point for some real nice photos and go-pro videos. Not sure how they decide on who sits there, but you can ask. On helicopters you pay extra for the front seats but that's not the case with the planes. My wife sat in the 'passenger' section, and the views there were amazing as well.

As one of the other reviewer said, you get a small momento after the flight, and we got the same. Really nice touch.

Recommendations: look at the forecast a couple days in advance and book accordingly. We had a nice sunny day and that made the ride. If it's cloudy, I'm sure it won't be the same. Ask for a right-side seat, or even the co-pilot seat if possible.

Needless to say, we would fly with them again if we visit in a few years' time, and would recommend these guys with out hesitation.

Review Title: This will be your top Kauai / Hawaii experience!
Review Text:
We went on the 4 p.m. Cessna ride on Thu, 10/9, the latest flight of the day. This plane ride was phenomenal! We visited the island as part of the Norwegian Cruise Line, Pride of America cruise. This is not an excursion offered by NCL, we found it courtesy of Google and are so glad we did! We originally were looking for a helicopter tour when we fortunately stumbled upon this incredible alternative. Our homework paid off.
Riding in the Cessna with Wings over Kauai offered several great advantages. 1) This was effectively a private tour - it was the pilot, my wife and me. 2) I love photography. The pilot allowed me to open the window to take glare-free photographs of the spectacular views offered by the plane. (See several scaled down photos below) 3) We spent a fraction of the cost of a helicopter tour. 4) It's hard to imagine a helicopter tour topping this one. 5) The pilot, Josh, was very skilled and professional, had a wealth of knowledge about the island and was extremely personable. His easy going demeanor quickly put us at ease and set the tone for a an incredible flying experience. 6) This is a family owned business. The owner gave us a ride back to the cruise ship - a personal touch we wouldn't expect from the larger helicopter companies. 7) The incredible Napali Coast is only accessible by air or water. Since the cruise ship takes you by the coast, we were able to see the coast from both perspectives. Viewing it by air is much more dramatic and impactful. If you are going to Hawaii, Kauai is a must-see island. If you are going to Kauai, the Napali Coast is a must-see destination, so we recommend seeing it the best way possible - by air!
It's a shame NCL doesn't offer this as one of their shore excursions - so many cruise passengers are missing out. On the other hand, if it was an NCL offering the price might be much higher, so it will pay great dividends for the traveller (cruiser or non-cruiser alike) who does their homework.
If you are visiting the islands via NCL, you will arrive in Kauai on Thursday at 8:00 a.m. and leave on Friday at 2:00 p.m. If you take this flight on Friday, do so earlier in the morning so you don't risk missing the boat that afternoon. We chose to take the late Thursday afternoon flight in lieu of the only NCL offered luau Thursday night. What a great decision! Because half of the ship's cruisers were off-ship attending the luau, we returned to the ship, ate supper in a much quieter restaurant, then had the pool completely to ourselves for over an hour!

Review Text:

Time wise, you get the biggest return on investment if your time on the island is limited. In one hour, you get to see so many amazing views of this island that are not feasable by foot, boat, or car. The center of the island is just so incredibly breathtaking. You will see miles of amazing vegitation and waterfalls with no human life... it's truly something I've never seen before.

I suffer from motion sickness (in fact, we took a boat ride/ snorkeling excursion on which I got queezy despite taking Dramamine) and had NO PROBLEMS AT ALL on Wings Over Kauai. My biggest challenge was nervousness which was much eased by Capt. Josh and Dori. The service is so friendly and personal. Dori gave us a great overview of our trip and made us feel so welcome. Capt. Josh made us feel comfortable, casually describing his experience as a pilot (having flown both large planes for major airlines and flying small planes as well) and often referring to us by name during our flight, often checking up on us and even wishing me a happy birthday!

I took Dramamine an hour before the flight. They offered ginger candy and water/soda on the plane. Views from the right we're better as many other reviewers mentioned. I have a small threshold for comfort when it comes to temperature and the ride was not too hot, not too cold but juuuuuust right. Review Text:
We took a plane tour over Kauai with WOK in September. We have been to Hawaii seven times having visited Oahu, Big Island, Maui and Kauai. Easy to say Kauai is our favorite, as it is a very beautiful, restful island. We enjoy the beaches, swimming, snorkeling. We have seen more sea turtles, rays, dolphins, etc. here than anywhere else. We have been in awe of the Na Pali coast on catamaran trips (Capt Andy is the best), but this trip we tried another method of enjoying the beauty of the island. Yes, Wings Over Kauai.

The staff is super friendly. We flew with owner/pilot Bruce. Don't be concerned about flying in a comparatively small plane. I have been in several choppers, private seaplanes, small commercial planes, private jets, etc. over the years and my flight with WOK was probably the most relaxing, smoothest flight I have had. Credit to Bruce. We all agreed it was like floating on a pillow.

And Bruce's talents are just not as a pilot. As a professional biologist you can absorb an education on the island as you absorb the awesome beauty of the island. Words can't even come close to what your eyes will experience. I found myself quiet, unable to speak, and just trying to capture the moment.

Tripadvisor only has 1 - 5 stars, otherwise I would rate this higher. It is one of the best activities I have taken in all my trips. Be smart, call, make a reservation. Bring a camera, and you can continue to enjoy the beauty for the months after your feet (unfortunately) are back on the ground. But don't look thru the viewfinder, put the camera on automatic and snap away. Don't cheat either of your eyes from a direct view!!

Bruce & WOK, THANKS, I will see you on my next trip for another flight.

Review Text:
I booked this flight during the planning stages of our Hawaiian Island cruise on the NCL Pride of America. Kauai was the final stop of our itinerary prior to disembarking in Honolulu, and I opted to fly with "Wings" as the last day in Port.

What an incredible experience it was to fly over this beautiful island and observe it from a totally different perspective. Words simply cannot describe the images and scenery as seen from the air... even my photos (over 200 taken) can't truly depict how breathtaking it is to see the island in this unique way.

Sadly, my wife passed on this experience, as did the other couple that was scheduled to fly... so it was just my pilot, Josh, and myself on board. Josh asked if I would prefer to sit in the co-pilot seat instead of in back... really? He had to ask? Seriously, what a treat it was to sit "up front" and become an honorary member of the crew. Unfortunately, that didn't entitle me to an employee discount :( But it did offer me an awesome view :))

I'd like to share some of the details about the flight, unfortunately, my description wouldn't do justice to the experience... so you'll just have to book a trip for yourself. I will say, we did get to see a helicopter on the ground near the north shore that had to land after experiencing mechanical difficulties, but that's another story.

I will say this; if I am fortunate enough to return to Kauai, I'm including some extra bucks in the budget for another flight with Wings Over Kauai... even if I don't get to be a member of the crew.

So, if you find yourself on the Island of Kauai, book a flight with "Wings"... you won't be disappointed.

Review Text:
This was the best experience we had during on stay on Kauai in August 2014! We had booked this flight many months in advance as this was high on our 'to do' list. It turned out that we were booked on the day that hurricane Iselle was to hit the island. As soon as I heard the timing of the hurricane, I called Wings Over Kauai to see if there was any possibility to be rescheduled. They were very understanding, and moved our flight up to 2 days earlier. We went up on a morning flight and fortunately it turned out to be a beautiful day! We saw incredible views of the island with its many waterfalls. The Napali coast was stunning. As it the summer, we were able to see many sandy beaches and entrances to caves. Our pilot, Josh (if my memory is correct) was extremely knowledgeable and pointed out the different places we were seeing along with some history of the island. The 3 falls of the 'Fantasy Island' falls can only be seen from the air. The aerial view of Waimea Canyon is just beautiful with its colorful red rock mixed with lush green vegetation. After seeing the entire island from an aerial view, it gave us a comparative perspective for seeing the island from a ground level view.

Several people that I have told about this experience have all said that they are 'afraid' to get on a small plane that seats 6-8 people. My husband, daughter (10) and I had never been on a small plane, but it was very smooth and it just felt like we were floating in the air. It was not scary at all! Our pilot had flown with American Airlines and was very experienced. We felt very safe! We purchased a video of our flight (cameras were mounted on the plane's wings) and had fun re-experiencing our adventure on DVD after returning home. You will not be disappointed!

Review Text:
Awesome service. Our pilot, Bruce, made a point to keep track of all our names and interacted with each of us by name throughout the flight. A very nice touch. We actually flew through some rain (as might be expected as you approach the rainiest mountain on earth) and turbulence didn't get uncomfortable. They had assured us that if they had to cancel due to weather that we would not be charged for the tour at all. It is true that everyone gets a window seat but the nature of an airplane is that it doesn't turn on a dime. They essentially have to choose to go around the island clockwise or counterclockwise. They choose clockwise, so those on the right hand side of the airplane get the best views. If you fill the plane, there will be 2 guests on the right and 4 on the left. They do fly across the middle of the island, turning inland over Poipu going up Waimea Canyon and then out over the ocean for the trip down Na Pali. He does do a full circle over the most beautiful section of Na Pali so everyone on the plane gets a view. He then flies to the left of Ke'e beach and Tunnels then turns inland over Princeville for a nice view of the waterfalls coming off the mountains there. They don't fly as low as helicopters do, but I wonder if helicopters take you over the entire island. (I think they may have to focus on one area or another.)

Overall a great trip for a fraction of the cost of a helicopter trip.

We chose airplane over a boat trip because we feared Captain Andy's from Port Allen would be too choppy and the risk of getting seasick was too high. Also we heard the Port Allen route gives you too short of a visit to the Na Pali coast.

Thanks, Bruce!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
We have nothing but good things to say about this outfit.

I tried to book online but everything looked full and I was working on my smartphone which made it difficult. I gave up and called, and Ellen was helpful and patient with me, and let me know how to go about booking.

We got our flight scheduled (for the next day!) and followed the specific driving directions provided on the email confirmation. They took us right where we needed to go, and we were met by a friendly and helpful Bruce, who showed us to the waiting area and gave us some interesting reading material about the island.

Josh, our pilot, then came out to greet us, point out our plane, and let us know they were almost ready for us.

Shortly thereafter Abi greeted us and got us all set up for our flight. She let us know exactly what to expect and answered all of our questions. It turned out I HAD done something wrong trying to book via smartphone but Abi made it no big deal and corrected my error. She was helpful and friendly and then took us out to the plane where she and Josh helped us board.

Josh was great. He was very personable, answered all of our questions, and clearly knows how to pilot a plane. He said he flies several times a day several days a week, but he never made us feel like we were just a number. He was friendly and helpful, answering our questions that weren't even related to the flight or the island -- like where to get the best steak -- but that will remain our little secret. :-)

We highly recommend Wings Over Kauai. Our 14 year old son thought it was "really cool" and our 16 year old daughter couldn't believe how quickly the 65-70 minute flight went by. My husband and I were simply stunned by the beauty and enjoyed learning more about the island.

We felt the length of the tour was perfect, and--although not mechanics--felt the plane was in great condition and it was clean and tidy. We didn't do a helicopter tour due to some motion sickness two of us experience sometimes and we think this was a good decision. One of us was fine and the other experienced mild discomfort which was helped by some ginger chews provided by Abi.

Oh! We did the Airvan charter so we didn't have to share our plane and it cost $500 for the 4 of us + a tip that was not required but we happily gave. Enjoy Kauai! Aloha!

Review Title: Highly recommended...  better than a sunset cruise
Review Text:
So the BF and I were debating whether to view the Na Pali Coast by water or air. I made the executive decision to do both. We did the cheaper sunset cruise with Captain Andy's the night prior. This by far, was a much better, unique experience.

I know most people do the helicopter tours but those were much more expensive and I was wary about riding in a helicopter hovering over places like that and the loud noise. Besides that, this place came highly rated on Trip Advisor so this was the choice for us.

The family that runs this company are very professional and courteous to a T. Upon booking, I think I spoke with Bruce who was super friendly and helpful over the phone. I hung up with a good feeling about them.

We were running slightly late because we took a wrong turn at the airport and had to circle around so they called us just as we were parking the car. Dori was still very nice about it. They called me to the back office and introduced themselves to me, each of the 3 people, shaking my hand. I work in customer service so I make a note to commend them on that.

They gave me a kukui nut lei and a small white flower (I think it was a tuberose) to put in your hair. It smelled wonderful but you can't really wear it on your ear since you have to wear the headphones on the plane so I ended up sticking it in my purse. My boyfriend oddly enough, did not get any gift so I thought that was strange. Another couple was there and the man was wearing the same kukui nut lei I had and the woman had on a different kind. I suspected that they gave it to her but she may have already been wearing one. Anyway, that was the only thing that bothered me about their service. They should equally be accommodating to the males.

I agree with a prior review I read about doing this towards the end of your trip so you can see the places you have been to previously by land. It gives you a better frame of reference and a greater appreciation of this beautiful island. There are no bad seats on the air van. Each seat has its own window. They seat you by weight. My boyfriend sat next to the pilot and I sat directly behind my boyfriend but I was fine with that. They also provide drinks, at least mini water bottles and ginger candies in case you are prone to motion sickness.

The flight itself was outstanding. Our pilot/guide, Josh, was super knowledgeable about everything and even answered all the curious questions we had about various things we saw. The views were spectacularly awesome and they even had a soundtrack during the trip, sometimes corresponding to the view (i.e. - the Jurassic park music). That was a GREAT, very much appreciated touch.

They take photos of you in front of the airplane before you take off and email it to you for free. Make sure the other passengers are not in the back photo-bombing your picture with their legs on the other side of the plane like ours had. They have a video of your specific flight for sale if you want it but they gave us generic one for free! :)

Loved it! A must do!

Review Text: What a great experience!  Our hosts for the day included pilot Josh, his lovely wife Dori, and their very cute dog Millie. Review Title: Fantastic flight, great people and the best bang for your buck
Review Text:
We booked Wings Over Kauai as part of a package between them and Blue Dolphin Charters to see Kauai from both sea and air. We did them both the same day, which I'm not sure I'd try again, but we had limited time on the island. The boat tour went about an hour long, so while we did manage to stop by our hotel and change, we were rushing a bit to get to the airport. As it turned out, there was no need to do so. There were two friendly folks there who got us checked in and chit-chatted for a while until the rest of our group arrived. The pilot came out and talked to us, saying weather had come in over the Na Pali coast and that we probably were not going to be able to see it very well. They offered to cancel or re-book our tour, or gave us the option of seeing what we could. Since we had done the boat tour of the Na Pali coast that morning, we decided to go ahead and go up.

It was just me, my husband and another couple (coincidentally also from our boat tour), along with the pilot in the tiny plane. They set us up with water, soda and ginger chews for motion sickness (just in case). We also had noise-canceling headsets and microphones to talk to each other and the pilot during the flight. We ended up seeing almost the entire island and only hit really heavy rain at the end. We were able to see most of the coast, amazing views of Waimea Canyon and the famous waterfall from Jurassic Park, along with lots of other things. The pilot's information was entertaining and interesting, and the musical background was a bit cheesy, but fun and added to the tour.

Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend this. For $225 for the 6-hour boat tour and 90-minute flight it was well worth it. They took our photo in front of the plane before the trip and printed it on a DVD with highlights from the flight (generic, not our specific tour) and gave us that for free at the end of the flight. There was an option to purchase a Blu-ray or DVD of our specific flight, shot from several Go Pro cameras in and outside the plane, but we opted out of that. There was no hard sell. Great people and a great tour!
