Review Title: This is the must do activity for Kauai
Review Text:
There's a reason Wings Over Kauai Air Tours is the # 1 rated activity for Kauai. My wife and I recently returned from our 2nd visit to Kauai. Having been stationed on Oahu and trained on the Big Island, I can say Kauai is the most beautiful Hawaiian Island. Wings Over Kauai is the BEST method to see the landscape. During our most recent visit, we took my wife's parents and her older brother. The hour long air tour was the highlight of our group's excursions.

We booked the one hour Air Van Private Charter, and Josh was our pilot / guide while airborne. Dori, Ellen and Millie (the owner's dog) greeted us at the hangar that is shared with several smaller air tour operators. The easiest route to their hangar is drive towards LIH (Lihue airport), pass the curbside pick up and drop off and you'll see the fixed wing hangar less than a mile on the right side. Keep LIH runways on your right side, and you'll see the Wings Over Kauai signage. Check-in consists of weigh-ins for aircraft balance, a model of Kauai to point out routes (each dependent on weather), and addressing any concerns passengers have pre-flight. Once check-in was complete, we had ample time to use restrooms on site and view aircraft departing and arriving into LIH.

Prior to boarding the aircraft, a group photo was taken plane side. GoPro cameras are mounted to each wing and at least one interior camera faces passengers. My wife was given a Kukui nut necklace for the photos and as a gift. Once on board, BOSE two-way headphones are given to each passenger for communication with your pilot and each other. For airplane enthusiasts such as myself, you'll enjoy hearing ATC and other aircraft in the area during the flight. I really liked this feature as you'll quickly notice all the aircraft circling Kauai are constantly in radio contact and sharing information regarding weather or terrain features. A cooler with refreshments and snacks is also provided in the cabin, a nice touch. Highlights of our flight included two whale pods sighted on windward side of the island, breathtaking views inside Waimea Canyon and the beach views from 5,000 feet. We even passed over our condo in Princeville and took photographs to share with future renters, review forthcoming.

Total airtime was over 60 minutes, and the blend of Josh's commentary and background music was perfect. Everyone on board had questions for Josh, and he did a great job explaining the island's legends, culture and environment. As we taxied back to the hangar, a DVD or BluRay copy of your flight is offered. The 3 GoPro cameras capture everything you saw during the flight, and interior commentary is optional. Dori gave us a CD with their promotional video and the cover included one of our group's pre-flight photos. Ten minutes after we landed, my smartphone showed an e-mail from Wings Over Kauai with five group photographs Dori took. Customer service is above and beyond at Wings Over Kauai.

Why Wings Over Kauai Air Tours vs. helicopters or other guides? The seating is spacious, and you have more flexibility in where you can place passengers. All passengers have a port and starboard window. Driving into Waimea Canyon doesn't guarantee a view, we've made that drive before. My mother-in-law opted out of the flight just prior to departure. The ground crew never made her feel guilty and were supportive of her decision. You cover more airspace vs. the helicopter tours, and you literally fly above them. The tour is priced extremely well, and environmental impact is low. Don't hesitate to call or e-mail Wings Over Kauai for assistance in planning. This is the must do activity for Kauai! Mahalo Wings Over Kauai!

Review Text:
Quick info about us: We are a family of four, husband and wife for 16+ years and twins (boy and girl born in 2001). Our daughter is the social butterfly, our son has autism (he is non-verbal, but loving and happy). Our travels are interesting because they always have the perspective of a family with a special needs child as a part of them.

Having been to Kauai twice before, we were debating what to do for our final hurrah of this trip with our kids. The trip had been beyond fantastic for our family after a long and stressful year. Since we have taken boat trips to tour the Na'pali Coast twice before, we wanted to do something different. We narrowed it down to an ATV tour, a helicopter tour, or the Wings over Kauai tour. I like to email companies before signing up to explain our son's autism and to share our uncertainties on how he will handle certain activities. This helps me both get more information and also hear the heart of the company's response. Wings over Kauai began to win hands down right off the bat with Ellen's thoughtful and kind emails. You don't know how heart warming it is to have compassionate people communicate to you when you are vulnerable about your child's special needs! Even though we doubted how good an hour flight could be, we decided to choose Wings over Kauai based on three things: 1. Ellen's emails. 2. Tripadvisor's reviews. 3. Affordable price. It was the best decision we made amongst a two week string of great experiences!

When we arrived, the staff (Ellen, Ellen's daughter and a friend, and Bruce) all greeted us warmly and were delightfully personal and friendly. After a review of procedures and our tour, we were raring to go. By this point our son had seen the airplanes taking off and landing and was getting very happy and excited that we were going to go on one! Josh, our pilot, talked with us before we boarded (we got the family photo as well), and we loaded up in a way that seemed to work best. We left our son's microphone unplugged in case he got worked up, but left it to where he could hear us. Again, to have people concerned about your son is a huge blessing, and we felt that they went above and beyond to care.
The flight itself was everything people here have said. It gave us a whole new perspective of the island and it's beauty and made us love it all the more. Josh was the perfect host with lots of information and stories and insight that added great depth to the experience. He was very personal and by the end of the tour it felt like we were lifelong friends. The island itself is the most beautiful place I've been, and this tour showed off that beauty tremendously.

When the flight was over we felt that it was just the right amount of time, but also felt that we could take the tour over and over again just because it was so beautiful and informative. We took one last picture and our boy had a huge grin on his face. We were given the complimentary dvd and it was great to have such a personal touch of having our photo on it.

Since it has been 8 months since our adventure, I can still say this is a memory we are glad we made. Our son (now thirteen) still often pulls up the picture of the Wings over Kauai plane and points to it (his way of asking to go again). I agree buddy, I agree!

Review Text:
We were in a time share for most of our trip and we were debating on a helicopter ride or a plane ride knowing they were both great ways to see the island. We decided to go with Wings over Kauai so we could see the Na Pali coast from the air and also be able to do a boat trip and see it from the water. The plane ride was amazing and we did it at the end of our trip and we were able to see so many places that we had seen from the air. We could not asked for better weather and decided to go in the afternoon based on a recommendation from where we were staying.

Bruce and his wife were great from the beginning until the end. Just going through some of the photos and the shots that I took from the plane came out great. I am so happy that we decided to do it and it was worth the money spent - I guess the only thing that we could have had with the helicopter is the ability to hover but I am not sure if we would have seen more for the higher cost.

Well worth it!!! Before we left they took a photo of us and when we got back we were presented with a CD that had our photo on it that they had taken along with highlights from the tour that were taken at another time - but still they were spots that we had seen on our tour. Review Title: Most bang for your buck, Wonderful Route, Great People and Beautiful Island
Review Text:
We were on the Norwegian Cruise Line Hawaiian trip. The ship stopped at Kauai for two days. The helicopter ride ship was promoting costs around $350 per person. Since I have a group of 6 with varying budgets, I Tripadvisored and found Wings Over Kauai. For the whole 6-seater plane and an hour long tour, it costed us a little more than $500 after taxes in TOTAL. And it was basically a private tour.

The flying route will take you to all of the main attractions on the island of Kauai. Na Pali Coast, the Waimea Canyon and all the wonderful waterfalls, etc. We were very lucky with the weather, so the oldest of Hawaiian Islands, Kauai was completely revealed to us. After seeing most of the main islands, I have to say it is the most beautiful in my eyes.

But, really it is the people of Wings Over Kauai that truly made this tour so special. Started from the booking, planning, pick-up and finally the tour itself, everyone involved was courteous and very helpful. Ellen handled most of the pre-flight arrangement, she knows about our ship better than I did. As it was to leave earlier than I thought I would on the day of the trip. And most of all, Josh our pilot, was really knowledgable and have this genuine friendliness about him that just made all of us enjoyed our trip so much more. The fact he speaks some Chinese and good looking just made my mom and all of her friends felt very much "at ease" (they were really worried about the size of the plane when I told them about the tour). They ended up spending all of the preflight time chatting and teasing Josh and totally forgot about their initial worries (it went so bad as one of them was asking if he'd like to be set up for a date with her daughter. at which point I had to intervene :). Since he use to be a commercial pilot for the American Airline, he handled our 6-seaters with ease and professional smoothness. Even my partner who usually gets really nauseated with a small plane, barely had any problems this time. And the landing was very smooth, I clapped. As a tour guide, Josh was equally up to the task. One thing I really loved, he had different the background music ready when flying over different locations.

All in all I thoroughly enjoyed the tour, it was hands down the least expensive and the most exciting tour we did on the whole Hawaiian tour.

Couple of tips:
1)Book ahead, if possible with a group of 5-6 or 2 for the whole plane (they also have a two-seater). Otherwise, it's $125 per person as of Nov. 2013.
2)For pickup, ask for the Pier if possible. Although their pickup spot isn't too far from the Pier, it's about 5-10 mins walk and has a convenient store there that sells much cheaper items than the ship store.
3)The only downside with the plane tour is, maybe with a helicopter you can get closer to the scenic location. However at triple the price, I wonder it would be worth it any more.

Review Title: Breathtaking, peaceful, non-intrusive, and... something you should do
Review Text:
This is something I would recommend to anyone. And the small plane experience is perfect for it. We chose this instead of doing a helicopter tour because helicopters are so noisy and intrusive that they are called the "mosquitoes of the island" by some of the locals.

But you should do this tour for more reasons than the above. It's peaceful, breathtaking, and a wonderful experience. You see parts of the island that are otherwise not viewable. And they are as amazing. i don't want to give anything away, but it's worth the time and the money, far and away.

The staff is great - courteous, friendly, and open. Our pilot Josh was fantastic. The flight was smooth despite what I assume to be challenging conditions with the island's particular geography. He is very informed about the island itself, its history and significant landmarks and features, and imparts a great deal of interesting information throughout the tour, all while expertly managing the flight itself.

I highly recommend this to anyone. If you have a tendency toward motion sickness, of course do take some dramamine or whatever works for you as you might for a boat ride or similar.

Review Title: Yes, it is really THAT good
Review Text:
I can't add a whole lot to what other reviewers have already said, but this place is the real deal. They are super friendly and seem to genuinely enjoy what they do.

The plane ride is about 65 minutes long and every passenger receives noise-canceling headphones equipped with microphones that allow you to chat with other passengers on board. Our pilot, Josh, was very nice and offered interesting details about Kauai, while also answering any questions we had. He was helpful in pointing out the numerous waterfalls and beaches you'll fly over so you're not mindlessly scanning the island.

Unfortunately I got sick towards the end of the flight and had to use the "aloha bag" as they call it. Helpful hint: if you're about to get sick, point the microphone AWAY from you before you hurl. It was the first time I've ever gotten sick on a plane, but it was my fault because I had suffered heat exhaustion the day before and was still woozy heading into the flight. But the staff made me feel at ease and not ashamed at all. That was really nice.

We paid about $250 total for two people, not including tip. There are definitely cheaper alternatives out there but remember, they are rated No. 1 on Trip Advisor for a reason. If you are looking to splurge on a single excursion, this is definitely it.

I can totally understand why this tour is the number 1 thing to do in Kauai as per Trip Advisor. Its cheaper than helicopters and provides the same scenic views. Their customer service was top notch. Review Text:
My wife is not a good flyer, even on a 767, let alone a little Cessna or the like. There was no way I could get her on a helicopter tour, so the doors off experience wasn't going to happen. So I read to her very carefully, the reviews on the stability of WOK's Australian built plane, the safety etc, but she still wasn't having a bar of it. So I did what any good husband would, I booked it anyway.
So, one or two days prior, she began to go quiet and on the day of the flight, she couldn't even talk to our pilot, who was doing his best to appease her, but clearly failing. The only thing left was to just get her in the plane and do it.
Well, the flight was faultless, hardly a bump, even when warned of certain areas that may cause a bit of turbulence. The scenery is spectacular, the commentary informative, with an open mic if you want to ask anything at all.
I recommend you do this straight up, and then spend the rest of the time relaxing. We drove around a bit, hiked, but the view is unrivalled from the air. Don't miss this, as only 15 or 20% of Kauai is accessible by road. It is The best way to see the NaPali coastline. We hiked up the Kalalau trail from Ke'e Beach on a very calm day and watched as the Catamarans and Rafts bounced and bounced all the way down the coast. We were so glad we cancelled our plans to "sail" down the coastline. It looked liked a bumper car ride. And I really don't know how you could get the same perspective as from the air. A lot of bouncing to zip through a couple of sea caves I think.
Plus, at the end, you can order a copy of your flight, recorded in 1080HD, complete with all your audio too, for $30. Great value. It costs about that for two digital photos off a Disneyland Ride doesn't it. And don't worry about the clouds. We went on a very cloudy day, which it always seems to be, but saw everything, but the top of the peak of course. Great value. Book it now.

Review Text:
My boyfriend and I experienced more of Kaua'i during our hour with Bruce than in our four days on the island. We took the Wings Over Kaua'i flight on our first day, so the overview gave us a good idea of how we wanted to spend our remaining time.

Pros follow:

*Private tour in a four-seater propeller plane (Bruce, the boyfriend, me)
*Boyfriend (as "co-pilot") ticked off pre-take-off checklist as we watched an American Airlines plane depart before us
*Bruce smoothly handled the plane, so we didn't experience any motion sickness
*As we circled the island, Bruce listed the places we could explore during our time on Kaua'i (e.g. Anini Beach, a lagoon like spot), which was materially more efficient than reading a travel guide
*Views of waterfall after waterfall that are unaccessible except by air

This tour was really good value, and I appreciated the funds go to a mom-and-pop business operated by people passionate about Kaua'i. Frankly, $125 per person is a steal, and I'd recommend this tour without reservation to any of my friends heading to the "Garden Island."

If you decide to do one thing during your time here, this should be it!

Review Text:
After reviewing a number of air charters, we chose Wings Over Kauai based primarily on the Number 1 rating here at TA, plus the excellent reviews from previous customers. It is also cheaper - by half, at least - than a helicopter tour (for the same 60-75 minute tour), and if you are eco-minded, apparently the fixed-wing aircraft of Wings uses much less fuel than a copter. Though it seems that all the companies offering air tours have terrific safety records, it is also my belief that fixed-wing aircraft are generally safer than helicopters. We are joining with all those who have given Wings an excellent rating with no hesitation, and provide our recommendation with great enthusiasm!
From the moment we arrived at the airport, we were made to feel welcome and at ease, should we have had any anxiety. We conversed with the receptionist, who was the owner's daughter, and she was terrific. She handled the few administrative details with efficiency and again, made us feel extremely comfortable. She also took our photo before we boarded the plane, which was much appreciated.
Our flight had another couple, and all four of us had window seats (all the seats are window seats, but based on the flight of the aircraft, it appears that you may have better views of things by being seated on the right side of the airplane, as we all were able/instructed to do). Water and soda was available if you wanted it, as well as some remedies for motion sickness, if the need arose (my wife actually felt a little queasy during a portion of the flight and took one of the lozenges provided, which made her feel fine almost immediately).
I have flown in helicopters several times (all for work) and never in a small plane, so I was anxious to compare the distinctions between the experiences. I was immediately struck by the smoothness and quality of the flight, even in some mild turbulence. Our pilot was extremely knowledgeable and friendly, and something about his manner in the airplane exuded confidence (which is important in a pilot!).
The views from the airplane were simply amazing. The mountains, beaches, canyons, waterfalls, and caves were astounding in their beauty and ruggedness. The view of developed properties (e.g., golf courses, plantations, hotels/resorts) was also outstanding. The flight path covered nearly the whole island (I am not sure why about 1/4 [-less? Generally, from east of Princeville to Lihue] of the island is not on the tour) and flew over all the spots you would care to see. Be prepared to take many, many photos, of course (One slight negative regarding this concerns the fact that you are taking your pictures out of a window - the views you get through the window are amazing, but some photos are subject to get a little glare - not the fault of Wings; just be aware of this).
Once we landed, we were given a copy of a DVD which highlighted the views we experienced during the flight (these are "stock" clips, but still provide a nice memento of the trip - the cover of the DVD is one of the photos taken of you before you board the plane). Later that evening, the owners contacted us via email to thank us and encourage our review on TA (a nice touch!).
We met another couple at a luau a couple days later who had flown with Wings a day after we did. They flew when there was much more rain in the mountains, so they shared how the pilot stated they were seeing more waterfalls than were present in the days beforehand. I mention this to say that I don't think weather will likely stop your flight (this is up to Wings, but I think it likely that you will encounter rain at some point during the flight - this was no problem and didn't really diminish the quality of photos that we took).
It seems that all the travel folks recommend seeing Kauai by air during your visit. I think this is a valid recommendation, and I can say with no reluctance that you will not be disappointed by booking with Wings Over Kauai.

I know it's a pretty penny to be spending, but if you're going to Kauai, you don't want to miss this!

Review Text:
Given the support already on TA, this may seem like piling on but...no problem, lets pile! We have been not quite annual visitors to Kauai for many years and thought we knew the place pretty well. One thing we had never done was a helicopter or fixed wing tour. Should have done it way earlier, and this is definitely the way to do it.

We met Bruce the day before after a long day (his) but he was friendly and enthusiastic. Happy to talk about what WOK had to offer and talk about how that fit in with our hopes and expectations. We signed up for a C172 flight the next day.

Everyone has the same island to display (about which more later.) What was truly wonderful about Bruce, Sherry and the team is that this was a personal thing that, within the limits of what was possible, was the product of getting what we wanted done. I have spent a lot of time flying so I wanted to do a bit of hands on stuff but didn't want to miss all the sightseeing opportunities. No problem. Bruce was happy to fly the airplane when I wanted to sightsee and let me fly when I felt the itch. He is an instructor as well as a tour pilot so he can give a lesson along with the tour if anyone wants that.

Since we had been to Kauai many times, we also didn't need the pitch about "on your right you can see Poipu" etc. but we were very interested in information about places that are hard or impossible to get to on the ground. Bruce had all that at his fingertips along with a lot of fascinating stuff from his days as an agronomist on the island.

Bruce is fully capable of flying the standard tour and giving the standard spiel to first time, non-pilot visitors but he is also comfortable with adapting that baseline approach to whatever the customer actually would like. And that is what is truly neat about WOK. You don't feel like you are a participant in a script someone wrote ages ago and no one can vary from. It's more like a nice plane trip with a friend.

Josh and Sherry are from the same mould. They are friendly, helpful and anxious to do whatever they can to provide a memorable experience. When we got there, they were trying to sort out the larger plane which had booked one couple that was going to be a few minutes late and another who had to get back to their cruise ship immediately after an on time flight. They ended up moving the late couple to the next flight taking the time-constrained couple on a personal tour in the large airplane. A lot of companies would not do that!

In the meantime, Bruce escorted us to our small, "personalized" Cessna and we took off.

The fact that Kauai is one of the world's truly beautiful places was not news to us but the flight allowed us to experience it in an entirely new way. Trails we had hiked were now visible from above, as were dive sites that I had been to many times. It is just amazing to see the reef formations from a different perspective. They are beautiful up close but also beautiful in an entirely different way from 2,000 ft. The Napali coast is spectacular from the trail and from the ocean but present a whole new aspect from above (and beside.) Valleys that you basically can't get into at all on the ground are laid out below in awesome splendor. This is an experience not to be missed and that is true if this is your twentieth or your first and only visit to Kauai. We will add the memories to our Kauai databank and cherish them for a long time.

I have not done the helicopter tour so I can't really compare them but I was completely satisfied with the fixed wing experience. That is without regard to the price difference, which I am told is considerable. Since I would gladly have paid twice what we did for the experience, price was not a driver for us. We saw everything that was there to see and did it in the context of a friendly, personalized experience that we will remember with great fondness.

The other 1100 reviewers are dead on!

Review Title: Wings Over Kauai - Book it for sure!
Review Text:
Soaring over the island of Kauai with my boyfriend and Bruce, owner/pilot of Wing's Over Kauai, totally made my day.

We hit the jack pot -- we were the only ones who signed up for the 2:30 p. m. slot, so Bruce was our very own private tour guide.

Bruce took us up in his 4 seater Cessna. I've never ridden in such a small plane, but Bruce made us feel comfortable right off the bat.

We were up in the air before we knew it. What really impressed me about Bruce was his confidence and his concern for safety. There happened to be another tour company flying at the same time as we were and that pilot flew dangerously close to the Na Pali Coast mountains. Bruce made a comment that he would not do that, and that made me feel so much better.

There is nothing like the colors that you see on the island from the air. You can see why Kauai is called the Garden Isle. The hills and valleys were a vibrant green and the ocean shimmered a lovely turquoise. The Na Pali coast and Waimea Canyon was a sight to see, it was beautiful.

What was really fun was seeing those sights we had driven to on previous days. For us, Hanalei Beach was one of them. There's no mistaking Hanalei Bay with the half moon stretch of beach. Bruce pointed out many more pristine beaches to us that we will visit for sure the next time we are on Kauai.

Bruce was the best. So informative, so funny (he told some corny jokes too) and so endearing.

By the way, I have taken the helicopter tour before (about 10 years ago), but I enjoyed the Wings Over Kauai flight much better. Review Title: Incredible Way to See the Whole Kauai
Review Text:
We love this air charter tour company and have taken their tours several times while on Kauai. Most of Kauai is not viewable because of the terrain, so seeing the island by air is a must at least once while on the island. Wings Over Kauai offers a comfortable air tour of the entire island with spectacular views of the most popular and breathtaking sites the island has to offer, including: waterfalls, coastlines, Waimea Canyon, the inner island, sugar plantations, resort areas, and open sea.

On our last trip, we were thrilled to see several pods of whales swimming in the open sea from the air. Incredible! Throughout the ride, you'll hear about the island (including some history) from the friendly pilot through noise-cancelling headphones. The plane is small, carrying only about 8 passengers and they are always on time with their flights. Be aware that harsh weather will sometimes interrupt the tours, so it's a good idea to call ahead if the weather looks ominous. The flight leaves from the Lihue airport - very easy to find their hanger, just past the main terminal.

The plane tours offer a much more affordable way to see the island, as opposed to the helicopter ventures. Wings Over Kauai also gifts you with a lovely DVD as a thank you gift for taking their flight. My spouse and I will be watching our videos (both theirs and those that we took in flight) many times to remember this special trip. Highly recommended.

Review Text:
This review is for the Grand Deluxe tour with Kauai by Air. The tour covers most of the standard spots in Kauai including Jurassic Falls, Napali, Waimea Canyon, etc.

Experience (5/5) - The experience was amazing at every customer touch-point. Our initial conversation during the data gathering and reservation was candid, honest and direct without any high-pressure sales. This is followed by the first in-person conversation where they Bruce and Ellen warmly invited us into their office to collect additional information and address other flying logistics, rather than dealing with the customer at the counter. They are also well prepared with some interesting reading materials while the customers wait for the plane logistics to work out. The actual flying experience is amazing as well. Bruce is a very good pilot and guide who immerses you in the overall flying experience. He's extremely knowledgeable and beyond pointing the standard spots he understands Kauai's vegetation very well (he used to be an agro-scientist before). Finally, at exit they awarded us with a CD that had one of their tours on a bright & sunny day.

Pricing (5/5) - Fly by Kauai has one price, that is honored any way you contact them. This makes shopping far more easier. While doing our research, we came across groups that would change the price depending on the discount coupon/magazine you're holding.

Ethics (5/5) - I felt it was important to highlight this category because I've read nightmare experiences across some other reviews across their competition in Helicopter and Air. The case in point is where the second group did not show up due to a scheduling error. Bruce came by to tell us that they will need to change planes because the # of passengers had reduced. Unfortunately, their smaller plane did not have enough fuel and since it would take more time to refuel the plane they took us flying in the original larger plane, at the expense of their profit. A lesser group would have delayed the trip or made us wait longer till the smaller plane was refueled.

One other aspect I want to highlight is for people that get motion sick easily. I am one of those who feels nausea after an hour long boat ride. Given that, an Airplane ride is a safer choice rather than a helicopter ride as they tend to change altitude much more rapidly. So for all of you who get motion sick easily, I would recommend that you go for a plane tour. Note that this does not guarantee that you will not get motion sick, but it reduces the possibility.

Review Title: A highlight of your vacation that will provide fabulous photo memories!
Review Text:
We looked into doing a helicopter ride over Kauai, but while doing internet research, I came across 'Wings Over Kauai'. The reviews and the price seemed favorable and since we'd previously experienced a helicopter ride (on the Big Island), we decided to give the small plane a whirl. We were not disappointed!

We booked the flight a few weeks prior to our visit to Kauai in December 2012. 'Wings Over Kauai' has a convenient check-in desk at Lihue Airport where you check in with the friendly staff, go over some brief paperwork and then wait a short while in the small airport lounge where there are toilets available.

Josh, our pilot introduced himself and was bursting with friendly 'Aloha' spirit and confidence! We boarded the plane, where we got a complimentary bottle of water. We took off and as the runway disappeared behind us, the adventure began!

While in the plane, you wear headphones with a mic attached, through which you can hear the pilot's running commentary about what you're seeing. You can also ask questions and make comments that everyone in the plane can hear.

Have your long camera lenses ready for the stunning views as you see miles of coastline, blue waters, waterfalls, coffee groves, fancy resorts, celebrity houses, an Indian temple, the cruise port, the Na Pali coast, Waimea Canyon and possibly even whales.

It's a thrilling approximately 60 minute ride that will leave you on a high for a few days and provide you with some fabulous photo memories.

You are given a complimentary previously filmed short DVD as a keepsake of the trip and they e-mail you a digital photo of yourself next to the plane.

For $125 per person, it beat the price of the much more expensive helicopter rides and yet still provided one of the absolute highlights of our vacation. We recommend it!

NOTE: Complimentary parking available in front of the check-in terminal.
It's recommended you book the flight early in your vacation in case it has to be postponed due to weather conditions. We were lucky to have a beautiful clear day!

Review Title: Wings over Kauai - personal tour in Cessna
Review Text:
I was looking for something different to do while visiting Kauai'i for a meeting, so I looked about and ended up booking a tour via their website. Ellen got back to me not long after to confirm details. Very easy booking process, very friendly. Being a flight sim geek when i found out they could do a personal cessna flight with 'stick' time I had to jump at that chance! So I booked a personal flight in their Cessna (turned into an introductory flying lesson) which was excellent - so much so I bought a trainee pilot log book and booked another flight/lesson later that week!! The typical tours are in their larger Air-caravan with other people - i poked my head in it in the hangar while it was being maintained, looks like everyone gets a great view in comfort. (my second flight was at the end of day so ended at the hangar - so looks like they maintain their aircraft frequently. Interestingly Bruce asked me if it was ok if we taxied to the hangar - nice touch incase I was in a hurry), On both days while waiting for the Cessna, I saw people come off the Air-van and heard them all raving about how much they loved it etc.

The cessna is great for a personal/couples flight, and based on what i paid for a personal 1.1 hour flight/lesson in the Cessna, it was very reasonable indeed compared to a shared helicopter tour (i paid a bit over $200 for each personal flight/lesson of 1.1 hrs all the way round the island which is amazing value for what is effectively instructor time, hire of cessna and fuel - and I could have brought a guest along with me for no extra cost....). Granted a heli tour will get you a bit closer to the sights, but if you are looking for a very nice way to view all the sights of the island without the hairiness you will get from a helicopter tour, fly with this company. Even if you are zoned on a helicopter flight, take a tour with Bruce as well as you will get at least an hour to see the entire island (empty your camera's memory card!) at a leisurely pace with interesting commentary as well.

It is clear Bruce and Ellen love what they do, and Bruce was a very good tour guide with a background in agriculture on island prior to starting this company. Bruce was also a very good instructor - clear instructions, subtle assistance (or clear assitance where needed) and very informative incase anyone is looking to log some hours or just give it a try - cant think of anywhere better to do your first lessons, it is a stunnning island and the cessna seemed to be in very good condition. I am now begging my wife to allow me to continue lessons back home....

Very highly recommended.

Review Text:
I am going to write a big review as Wings over Kauai deserves it.

Background:
This is a must for any trip to Kauai. Choices are either a chopper or an air tour. The air tour is by far the most bang for your buck. For air tour we were on smaller Cesna so we were the only ones with our pilot - Josh, this is a great option for privacy and you get personal attention from the Pilot - I got to be the co-pilot :-). You can also choose a big 6 seater Airvan, which has larger windows but more passengers with you.
Tip: Sit on the right side of the plane.

Service:
Ellen was super courteous and made sure we had all the information about choices that we had. The lady at the reception (can't remember her name) was good too and did all the formalities. This process takes ~10minutes.
Tip: Try to book at least 4 days in advance.
Our pilot - Josh was brilliant and made sure this was a perfect way to say "Mahalo!!" to Kauai. He is extremely courteous and knowledgeable about the island. He made sure that we had every opportunity to photographs amazing vistas - he did double rounds over some waterfalls. The good thing about Cesna is that you get undivided attention of the pilot.
Many thanks to Josh.
They take your photos (and email them to you) before boarding on the plane and do a great job of tucking you nicely. I was the co-pilot, so i had an opportunity to see all the controls apart from enjoying the views. You get noise cancelling headphone so that you can communicate with each other and the pilot. They also give you a free pre-made DVD (not of your actual flight). It is a 5 minute DVD with music encapsulating the tour.
Tip: The photography buff should sit on the back seat as there is a bar blocking good photography over the front seat side windows.

Flight:
Our flight was around ~65 minutes. The flight started from Lihue commuter's airport terminal. The path started from the south-east corner of the island through Poipu beach, port Allen - into the center of the island Waimea canyon with all the waterfalls - into the north-west corner Napali coast and all amazing vistas - onto north-east side and finally back to the airport. The views are simply breath taking and no review can do justice for this experience. So you have to experience it yourself.

Bottom Line:
I would give A+ to Wings over Kauai for the price ($125/person) and the over all flight experience. You can choose a chopper ride that will cost you 2X ($250/person), the only plus on the chopper ride is that they can land you on some waterfalls which are otherwise inaccessible and can fly little close to the mountains. To me i wanted to get the big picture so flying close to mountains would make sense. However, both options are good.

Thank you WINGS OVER KAUAI for making this a memorable trip.

Bruce kindly let me (the pilot) fly out of the left seat and guided me around the island traffic pattern, while we flew around the coast, the canyon and the mountains. Bruce pointed out interesting landmarks and locations where famous movies have been shot. We chatted about various issues related to mountain flying, strategies for monitoring traffic and bird avoidance.

In the second flight Bruce kindly let us open the right window to get clear photo shots, free of reflections and distortions. He positioned the aircraft at an appropriate distance, and considered the direction of light for good shot opportunities. It is clear that he understands the needs of a photographer. He encouraged me to take control from the right seat (with which I did not have much experience) and all worked out well.

Bruce is an excellent pilot and an excellent instructor and quickly finds the level at which his student functions, communicates and encourages at an appropriate level. Ellen runs the office professionally and in a personally attuned way. All aspects of the experience have been pleasant. We look forward to more flying with Wings Over Kauai in the future and highly recommend the experience as safe, educational and adaptive to individual likes, needs and skill levels (pilots).

Review Text:
I am a very bad flier. Very nervous, can't handle turbulence, etc. So when my husband asked if I wanted to go on a flight on a very small plane through Wings Over Kauai I wasn't exactly sold...

Booking a flight was easy and Ellen responded quickly to all of our emails. She also sent perfect directions so we arrived at the terminal and parked with no issues.

When we arrived Ellen prepped us for the flight by giving us some tips and asking if we have issues with motion sickness (I do), then she gave me a beautiful kukui nut lei and took a picture of us in front of the plane.

She helped me get situated in the front of the plane and gave me peppermint and ginger chews to help with motion sickness. They also have small bottles of water on the plane.

Bruce was our pilot and he was amazing. He's very calm and knows absolutely everything about Kauai so kept up a soothing commentary throughout the flight. I had a bit of a death grip on my chair every time we hit a bump in the air but as Bruce was so calm and in control it really helped me enjoy the flight much more than I thought possible. Takeoff and landing were very smooth and we were lucky to have a pretty smooth flight. The views are stunning and you get to see parts of the island you'd never easily be able to access otherwise, this is a must do on Kauai!

Review Text:
We flew out on a Monday afternoon.

We showed up without a reservation, and were able to book a tour for just two hours later. One thing I can smell from a mile away is fake "niceness". That is, when people are being nice because they want your money. These people were genuine. They wouldn't take our money until flight time, even though I offered to pay early. They wanted to know, and remembered our names. Everyone was positive and friendly. You got the feeling that they liked their jobs, and wanted you to have a good time.

The pilot lived on the island and was also an airline pilot. He wasn't just some "guy" with a license, he knew what he was doing, was highly skilled, and friendly. He had a genuine knowledge of the island, and enthusiasm for living there. The flight was smooth, we saw the entire island, and had a great experience. The free DVD with our picture on the front was a nice touch. The ability to talk to the pilot throughout the flight with the headsets was also great. Highly recommended.

My only criticism: I filled out an online form the night before, but they hadn't checked their email by 11am. So we had to make a second effort to make a reservation by visiting them at the airport personally. They should have checked their mail and called us before we left in the morning. A minor quibble for an otherwise excellent experience.

I would fly with them again in a second, and recommend that others do the same.

Review Text: As an American living in Japan, flight training is difficult to get because it's expensive...and in Japanese. As such, both of my two training flights (so far) were done on vacation, first in Guam, then here at Wings Over Kaua'i. I have to say, Wings Over Kaua'i was at least 10 times better-- no exaggeration. The instructor worked with me and my specific needs-- NOT another island tour, but actual flight training. We went over to Port Allen, an uncontrolled field just SW of Lihu'e and practiced 2 touch-and-go's, went over the sea and practiced climbs, descents, stalls, and steep turns (my personal favorite). When we got back to the office, the people there were friendly and just as excited as I was -- you can tell they love their jobs. They even gave us a complimentary CD of our flight! Additionally, the CFI there was very helpful when I asked him about the right way to approach my training, and I ended up buying the FAA-authored Airplane Flying Handbook for just $20 -- only $2 over what the retail price was. All in all, an amazing experience...I'm looking forward to this Tuesday!

Review Text: We had booked the 11am flight but on waking on the appointed morning to low cloud and drizzle rolling in from the sea, we assumed there would be no flying done that day. But as quickly as the clouds had descended, the sun broke through and we found ourselves at the Wings over Kauai offices discussing the "flight plan" and safety briefing with owner Bruce, pilot Joshua and staff Sophia and Cathy. Due to the earlier unpromising weather, it turned out my wife and I were the only customers for the flight that morning so it was that we took to the air in the 4 seat Cessna. Just the two of us and Josh. And so the magic begins! Kauai from the air is absolutely spectacular. All flying, including by helicopters, is done clockwise so our route took us along the eastern shoreline, across the Waimea canyon and along the stunning Napali coast for a full 60 minutes in the air with expert and interesting commentary from Josh in between keeping in radio contact with the many helicopters whizzing around. In short, this is a must do tour for everyone visiting Kauai. Everything from the initial booking with Ellen to the final landing and personal friendly attention from everyone at "Wings" was faultless. Excellent value for money and even includes a personalised DVD of the trip in case your own shots aren't up to professional standards! Highly recommended.

Review Text:
These guys earned their 5 stars from the time of booking to the moment we returned to our car.

It was good to deal with a family run business and they certainly lived up to the high expectations that we had built up from all the TripAdvisor reviews.

The booking process with Ellen was efficient and really friendly. We're from the UK, with an 11 hour time difference, so everything was organised on line and by email. Responses came back by return, and provided all the information we needed. We booked our flight and were not even asked for a deposit. Ellen's response when we offered a payment was "we are just using the honor system to hold reservations and it seems to be working really well". A nice touch.

Our weather in Kauai was great but with some seriously strong winds and we were a little nervous about going up in a small 4 seater Cessner. Upon arrival at their office they assured us it would be ok, although they did warn us that there would be a few bumps! Before completing the paperwork and taking our money they suggested we speak with the passengers who were coming back from the previous flight. They offered to cancel the booking or re-arrange it for another day if we were concerned. There was no pressure on us whatsoever to fly, which we really appreciated. We eventually decided to go for it and are so glad we did.

Carter (Ellen and Bruce's son) looked after us while we were waiting, and was great. He then introduced us to Bruce, our pilot. Bruce's style is incredibly calming and he gave an excellent commentary on the landscape, history, flora and fauna, whilst chatting with us throughout the flight. He is not a typical tour guide, he is genuinely knowledgeable and interesting and clearly loves the island. The flight was amazing and we saw virtually everything. Kauai is absolutely stunning from the air.

After an extremely smooth landing, we went back into the office and were presented with a "home made" but good quality DVD of a typical flight, personalised with our photos, which had been taken as we boarded the plane. The photos were later emailed to us.

Having flown over Maui in a Blue Hawaiian helicopter a few years ago and been stuck in the middle seat, with limited visibility, I loved the fact that "Wings" only use the right hand seats of their aircraft to give everyone the best view. Also, the safety record of tour helicopters in Hawaii is not great and following the sad Blue Hawaiian crash on Kauai at the end of 2011, we felt a lot safer opting for a fixed wing plane.

A plane can't get into the valleys in quite the same way as a helicopter, but I remember from the previous flight that we spent a lot of time hovering and circling around so that everyone could get a view. With the fixed wing flight, it felt that we were getting a much better overview of the whole island, and at only 1,500 feet, the scenery still felt very close. It was just as good, if not better, than a helicopter.

We chose to fly with Wings primarily because of the safety issues and the seating arrangements. It was not really a cost based decision but, at about half the price of a helicopter flight, we thought it was amazing value for money.

Finally, having landed and been given our DVD, we walked back to our car and as we were getting in, Bruce made the effort to come over to offer directions and suggestions for the rest of the day.

We loved the personal and genuinely friendly service of Wings over Kauai and their professionalism throughout and recommend them one hundred percent.

Review Text:
We enjoyed our air tour of Kauai flying Wings Over Kauai in their six seater fixed-wing aircraft. Wings Over guarantees a window seat on the right side of the plane for every customer. This is crucial to getting a great view of the island from the air and getting your money's worth.

Bruce Coulombe, the owner/pilot, is a retired scientist and very knowledgeable. We thoroughly enjoyed his commentary and insights as we flew. Bruce is a veteran pilot with more than 5,000 flights over Kauai.

One drawback of the fixed wing aircraft is that it cannot get up close to many of the waterfalls and ridges that a helicopter can. For us, this was for the best because one of our party members tends to get motion sickness. Bruce and Ellen also made sure that the person with the tendency for motion sickness got to sit in the co-pilot seat to minimize the effects of the motion of the plane.

Review Text:
Ellen, Bruce and Joshua are a great team and make their customers feel welcome and relaxed. I had come to Kauai specifically to see the Na Pali coast by air (since i could no longer hike it). The fixed wing plane was good value and Bruce was a fount of information. The fixed winged plane does not go into the canyons but looking at helicopters that did, I was glad that the plane did not do that - a sudden gust of wind could be extremely dangerous.
Kauai is beautiful from the air and with so many contrasts it is a delight to see. We had seen the Waimea Canyon from the road the previous day and the plane view gave a wonderfully different perspective. Flying over Princeville and the northern coast was also lovely and gave us an idea of whether we wanted to visit there or not. If you are a golfer then there are some very interesting and beautiful golf courses.
Be ready with your camera and dont lean it against the window - it damages the windows. The opportunities for photographs are quick so you really need to be prepared. Video of the trip would be great. Bruce's son has produced a CD with photographs taken of customers before the trip and highlights of what is seen on a typical trip. A great souvenir. They also present the women passengers with a Kuki nut lei.
Bruce was an agronomist and is able to tell you all about the crops and flora of the island. The forest of abiza trees from Africa are beautiful - hopefully they are not an invasive pest.
We were lucky enough to see some waterfalls as there had been a lot of rain recently. The extinct volcano in the middle of the island has the highest record of rainfall in comparison with other parts of Kauai so there were quite a few waterfalls on he northern side.
Ellen provides air sickness ginger candy for those with queezy stomachs and cold drinks in the form of cola and water. Bruce goes through all the safety checks before take off including the use of life jackets.
The plane we flew had been made in Gippsland (Australia) and took six passengers as well as the pilot. It was comfortable. Note that the seating of passengers take place according to weight so you may not get the seat you had hoped for. However all seats have good views and Bruce will point out places and things of interest if you advise him before hand of your particular interests.
The fixed plane cost is roughly half the cost of a helicopter flight. It is good value indeed.
The waiting area looks over the helicopter landing area and you can sit in the open air and watch the helicopters taking off.
This was an event to remember and we will certainly be talking about for a long time to come.

Review Title: Not as good when it's Bruce's day off
Review Text: My husband and I visited Kauai in February 2012 with out toddler son and my parents. While there, my parents wanted to do something adventurous and saw Wings Over Kauai was the top attraction on TripAdvisor. My father called to see if any time was available during our last few days on the island and he was able to book a time for himself and my mother to go the next day. They went on the tour and came back to our hotel and just raved about the experience! They had a blast and thought that Capt. Bruce was wonderful and everyone there was so nice. They had such a good time that, even though I was scared to fly in a small plane, talked my husband and I into calling to see if there was any other times available for us to go. There was an opening two days later they were able to fit us in and while excited to go, I was very nervous too. Our flight time arrived and my parents dropped us off at the airport. I was still very nervous about the flight. Carter greeted us and checked us in, he was very nice. The flight before ours arrived back and my father quickly noticed it was not Bruce flying. Carter mentioned it was Bruce's day off. We were sad we didn't get to meet Bruce, whom my parents just raved about, but figured it would still be great. After checking in, we watched out the window as the pilot messed around with the plane hood up. It was not comforting to see that. Then we were taken out to the plane and seated. We met the substitute pilot (and now I can't even recall his name because I was too nervous) and got settled in the plane. The pilot then tried to start the plane and it wouldn't start. Now, I know nothing about planes so as a clueless passenger when a plane won't start, it is a little nerve-wracking. The pilot would try to start it and then we would have to wait about 5 mins and then he would try again. This went on for about 5 times and it finally started on what he said was his final try. I was about ready to demand to get off the plane when it started. And I noticed my parents and son looking out the window in concern as well when were weren't moving. Then I questioned the reliability of the plane for our flight and was basically laughed at by the pilot and another passenger. The flight itself was just OK. The pilot talked a bit about the sights below but really didn't have a conversation with us like my parents (and all the other TripAdvisor reviewers) said Bruce did. He knew I was clearly nervous but did nothing to make sure we felt relaxed. The views were beautiful and it was a nice time but I don't think it was even close to the same experience my parents had. The pilot was friendly but just didn't make it amazing like others mention when they talk about going with Bruce. I would recommend this tour to others but  would say to make sure Bruce isn't off the day they go. I completely understand that he needs a day off, just like everyone else, but they may need to teach the substitute pilot to offer a similar experience to the one Bruce gives. It was just night and day differences between two different tours in two days. I am still giving this a Very Good rating because I know how good it was for my parents and do think it was worth doing.

Review Title: You can't find nicer people to do business with!
Review Text:
Often one reads or hears great reviews and then can't help but be let down. Such was not the case with Wings Over Kauai unless you count being let down gently at the end of the flight. Before the flight, we were sent a map showing us how to walk from where our ship docked to the ABC store, and Ellen (one of the owners of the business) promptly picked us up at 9 AM in a nice van so all six of us in our group could travel to the airport together.

Our pilot Shaun couldn’t have been kinder. We were expecting Bruce, as we didn't realize the company had two pilots and had only read about Bruce, but Shaun was very competent and cordial and welcomed questions and also was cool about others pointing out nearby planes or helicopters, which is important for a pilot to be good about making people feel free to do.

Ellen also couldn't have been kinder. She gave me a kakua nut necklace for booking the trip (at least one woman from another plane tour booked by our group also got a lei) and gave all the females flowers for their hair, and took our photo by the plane and had that as a cover to a DVD on the highlights of their tour, which she gave for free to each party in our party of six who didn’t live with another party member (which meant 4 DVDs for our group!). She also supplied a ginger candy to each passenger to help with motion sickness in case anyone was susceptible to that (none in out plane were, but in one of our other two groups to go up, I think two or three were), and also gave us free waters.

The sights on this tour were amazing and made us feel like we need not bother driving to Waimea Canyon, so we scratched that from what to do after the tour and headed to Hanalei at Shaun's suggestion. Shaun doubled back over some spots to be sure people on both sides of the plane got to view things like a blow hole. The only drawback I saw of this tour was that the plane can’t dip into places like a helicopter can, so keep that in mind if you really want to get down into places (up close to falls and such). But also keep in mind that the Wings Over Kauai flight is far less expensive than a helicopter ride (it’s $520 with tax for a plane, so if you have only 4 people, it’s $130 with tax, but if you have six like we did, it was only $86.67/person, and the helicopter on Kauai will likely run you over $210/person) and the people simply couldn’t have been nicer, so I was pleased to do business with them.

Maren, their office worker, is also sweet as molasses and a pleasure to correspond with both via email and phone; she was also quite cute in making a typo and writing "vowel renewal ceremony" in an email, which resulted in my husband and I starting off our 25th anniversary vow renewal ceremony with a joke about how our ceremony was not a vowel renewal, even with how almost half the Hawaiian alphabet is comprised of vowels, as it's not about I or U, but about Aaaa and Eee and sometimes "WHY?" And I forgot "Oh" there, and oh, I also forgot that Ellen also allowed us to get a photo behind her counter at the airport (so we could pretend we were airport personnel and say, "May I have your boarding pass, please?") and once she got our second group of people up in the air, dropped us off at Alamo for us to pick up our rental. She also let us sit on the plane where we wished (though she will need to weigh each of you, she won't tell you your weight if you don't want to know) - we just had to make out a diagram showing where we each should be. Blue Hawaii Helicopters decide for people where they will sit. Another oh...Ellen also sent us our photos that she took in email with a nice thank you note. It's little touches like these which really make a business. None of the people in our group that went up on three planes in a row that day had anything but positive comments to make about the tour's views, service, etc. (just some sadly got a little motion sick, and that was not at all due to the pilot).

Review Text:
After reading other Trip Adviser reviews, we decided to take a chance on Wings Over Kauai. We were on the NCL-Pride of America 7/30 – 8/6. Ellen was great (and patient) as we swapped e-mails to work out a schedule that worked well for us and our itinerary.

We met Ellen at the designated location (ABC Store) and were quickly transported to the hangar where my wife was presented with a lei and a nice flower (a very nice touch). Paper work, a couple complementary pictures with the aircraft, a pre-flight check and we were off!

The inland area of the island was fairly overcast. Keeping safety first, Bruce did what he could to get us in the best places for the best views. As we traveled around the leeward side of the island, the clouds parted and the view of the Na Pali Coast opened up. It is hard to find words that can accurately describe the beauty of the Na Pali Coast—especially from the air. Breathtaking! The clouds started to subside as we headed inland. In one picture we can count 14 waterfalls (I’ll share it so you can see for yourself). Bruce answered every question asked of him and did a fantastic job keeping everyone engaged.

After landing, we were promptly presented with a DVD that had our picture on the cover (taken before we took off). It contained a video of the tour (previously filmed and produced to music). Ellen dropped us off at the shopping center where we met her (a short walk from the ship), but offered to take us back to the ship. We opted to grab a bottle of water at the ABC Store and walk back to the ship (with plenty of time to spare before the ship’s departure). On the walk back to the ship, I received an e-mail from Ellen that contained the pre-flight pictures (the same ones on the DVD) and a nice “thank you” note. Again, a very nice touch!

Bottom line, Captain Bruce, Ellen and Jeanne were great! Their #1 Rated Tour is not hype, it is for real! Courteous, professional, knowledgeable and safe! Treat yourself to this tour….you won’t regret it!

Review Text:

For us, on the day of our planned tour, the skies from Princeville looked gloomy and there were scattered showers, so I called Ellen because I was concerned. She immediately gave me the option to go later in the day which we chose to do, but the skies cleared beautifully anyway shortly thereafter. As an aside though, I saw several helicopters flying through rainy and gloomy skies that morning, which would have really stunk for the money they charge.
Bruce greeted us at the airport and everything ran so smoothly. The only issue is that we waited for another couple who had also reserved the flight, and they never showed, which held us up. In addition, they could have allowed someone else to reserve those seats, so if you aren't going to show, please provide common courtesy and make a simple phone call.
You will always get a window seat on this flight, and you will get to see everything there is to see in Kauai on a very comfortable, easy flight. There are fantastic photo ops, which is beneficial because the flight is slower and steady, and you are up in the air for around 70 minutes. Bruce is well informed about the island and points everything out there is to see--he's done the flight over 5,000 times.
This truly is a steal for the price, and turned out to be the highlight of our trip. Seeing the Napali coast by air turned out to be far better than by water, and having gracious, genuine hosts for our tour made it that much better...

The flight was about an hour and we circled the whole island while Captain Bruce, who I think is a genius, pointed out all kinds of land marks and told us facts and neat things about the area. One of the best things about this tour was when he showed us where they shot different clips from shows like Fantasy Island, Jurassic Park, Raiders of the Lost Ark, Six Days Seven Nights, and he even would help us so that we could get a nice photos. I got a really good shot of The Fantasy Island Falls from the opening scene when Tattoo was yelling "The plane, the plane." You see a lot of stuff that you normally would not see because you can not get to it by car. Hands down, this was one of the best things we did our whole trip. I would highly recommend it to anyone, especially if you can't afford the helicopter ride. I am so happy we did this. Thanks again Captain Bruce, Ellen, and Maren for this incredible adventure!

Review Title: Great for families, better than helicopter
Review Text:
We flew with owner and pilot Bruce of "Wings over Kauai", after he was recommended to us by our B&B the day before. It was fantastic, to say the least! Highly recommendable, especially for families of 3-6 who can have the plane to themselves (we went with my in-laws and our baby girl).
Guaranteed window seats also. I won't go into describing the views, they were truly amazing and hard to described with words.

Bruce and his wife Ellen have lived on the island for long and know it really well, they both have PhDs in agriculture and so we got to hear a lot of interesting stuff on the vegetation and history about Kauai. They are friendly and relaxed and run the small family show as a 'retirement' hobby, so its far from the expensive, highly commercialized and high-throughput tourist ripoffs you are likely to get with the helicopter operators.

We got a proper safety briefing before the flight, and could not have felt more comfortable before and during the flight. Free soda's and ginger chews were available against flight sickness, but we didn't need them.
Excellent in-flight communication system with Bose noise cancellation headsets, our 9-moth old daughter got soft baby earplugs and earmuffs on top, and slept straight through the 65 minute flight.

Discounts available or Hawaii residents or if you bring in a coupon.

The plane holds 6 people, but they rarely take that many up. We went up with just one other couple and the pilot, and once airborne, we all had a window seat on the right hand side -- something the helicopters can't give you. The plane is supplied with noise-canceling headsets and intercoms, and a cooler of water, soda, and even ginger candies for easily upset stomachs.

Once we were in the air, Bruce was a wealth of knowledge. He worked in agriculture (and even has a Ph.D), and is a long time island resident. He knew the history and the natural wonders of the island well and gave great explanations of the island flora.

We saw all of the sites, from the waterfalls to the Waimea Canyon to the breathtaking Napali Coast. We enjoyed every second, and Bruce's landing was the smoothest I've ever experienced. This is the one tour you can't miss on Kauai, and they even send you the photos they take afterwards via email -- free of charge.

In the end, this 70 minute flight allowed us to see so much more than the snorkel cruise would have and it even cost less. With the high-quality headsets on the plane, we were all able to talk to each other and everyone had the same view of what we were seeing since we were all on the right side of the plane.

If I had it do over again, the only thing I'd do differently is that I'd take this flight at the beginning of my trip so that we could visit some of the places that we saw from above but which I would not have otherwise known even existed.

Thanks Bruce.

Our flight with Wings over Kauai last week was a highlight of our vacation. The hundreds of positive reviews here on Trip Advisor don't lie: this is an excellent way to see all the beauty of Kauai.

I'm a bit of a nervous flyer and often have motion sickness. The Wings Over Kauai staff calmed my fears and helped us prepare for a great flight. The flight (we were in the larger plane, but it was just my husband & I) was very smooth taking off and landing. The staff let me know there might be some slight bumps as we moved from the Waimea Canyon area to the coast, but even that section was really smooth. They had a cooler with drinks and cold cloths to calm down motion sickness, but we didn't need either.

Captain Bruce was incredibly well-informed about Kauai: geography, history, geology, agriculture, movies, celebrities, beaches, hotels... you name it, he knows about it, and offers great explanations of what you're seeing and answers any questions you have. Unlike a few other people I interacted with on the trip, Wings Over Kauai's staff always gave accurate and appropriate answers. Bruce was also friendly. Some of it was certainly the same lines he gives every tour, but he was very open to answering our questions, and always called us by name (a nice touch).

Could you see the same things in a helicopter? Yes, I think you could. But, Wings Over Kauai offers a similar tour, at about half the cost, and without nearly as much motion-sickness potential. (All my friends who had visited Kauai told horror stories of being sick on helicopters; none of that with Wings Over Kauai). And, though they do weigh you (it's done discreetly) the weight limit isn't nearly as much of a concern as on a helicopter.

I can see why Wings Over Kauai receives such positive reviews! With so many parts of Kauai only visible from the air, you want to take a tour, and Wings Over Kauai is a most excellent way to do that.

Review Text:

Based on the reviews here, we decided to go on WOK as early as we could. However, it was cloudy on our first morning in Kauai. Since this was our first trip to Kauai, I didn’t know whether that was weather as usual (since it often rains in Kauai) or just a cloudy day. We arrived at the airport on time. Ellen’s first reaction was “you didn’t get my message”. Guess what, Ellen had called to suggest flying on other time. The cloud cleared up in the afternoon. I called again to check with Ellen. Ellen suggested if we went on the afternoon flight, we won’t get the flight for my own and the children would need to sit on the left side of the plane since she had rearranged other morning flight passengers to afternoon already. To make the long story short, Ellen keeps customer’s best interest in mind. That’s something very commendable.

We finally got on the flight on our last day. It was a beautiful day with blue sky. Kauai is as advertised as beautiful from the sky. You truly need to take a flight to see the mountain, valley, waterfalls and coastline. Since we had been to a few places already in Kauai, able to recognize places like Wailua Fall in the air was fun.

We all felt dizzy to different degree in the flight. The flight was smooth so it’s more due to our physical condition than anything else. Another thing, my video and pictures captured quite a bit of cockpit reflection. If you plan to take a lot of pictures and videos, beware of the reflection or don’t sit on the right co-pilot seat. The complementary DVD with our photo on the cover made up some from the glare. A follow up email is also a nice touch. WOK does not need to do any of these, but they do!

Overall, it is a wonderful experience and I will suggest taking this flight to anyone else.

Review Text:
For our 25th wedding anniversary, we really wanted to book a helicopter tour of Kauai. Steve and Lori from Tom Barefoot Tours TomBarefoot.com highly recommended booking a fixed wing flight on a Cessna from Wings Over Kauai. We're glad we took their advice. We flew with Wings Over Kaui on Thursday, July 15, 2010.

It's a true "mom and pop" operation run by Ellen and Bruce Coulombe. Both are very friendly, warm and accommodating. Ellen picked us up in town (we were on the NCL cruise ship Pride of America) and drove us to the airport. Flight check in was very smooth. She answered all our questions, even giving my wife a welcome gift and taking our photos in front of the Cessna.

My wife Maria was a bit hesitant to fly in a small 4 seat airplane. She told Bruce our pilot that she might feel queasy. Bruce put both of at ease with his wonderful suggestions for avoiding motion sickness. He also had on hand some ginger candies which his lovely wife Ellen told us were very effective in settling any upset stomachs.

Maria sat up in front, while I had the back all to myself. One great advantage of a fixed wing airplane is that you're guaranteed a window seat! Maria helped Bruce with the pre flight checklist.

This is a great way to see the island since you can't see it by car. Bruce pointed out all the must see sights and giving us his personal anecdotes as well. Bruce has a great sense of humour, a wealth of information and knowledge of Kauai, (he has a PhD in agronomy) and a masterful way of telling great stories.

It went by way too fast! This was a real personal tour. We highly recommend Wings Over Kauai for their unbeatable prices, longer flight time, and pickup and return if you're on a cruise or without a car.

Review Title: Bruce you were the best and provided a truly memorable experience.
Review Text:
My wife and I had a wonderful trip with Wings Over Kauai on Aug 13 during our honeymoon. Bruce, the pilot and owner, provided a first class tour with narration second to none. He involved all in the plane in the discussion and provided expert insight about Kauai, and its flora, that no one else could match.

Earlier in our trip we took a helicopter ride while on Maui and enjoyed that too. But after reading all the positive reviews in Tripadvisor about Wings Over Kauai, we thought a plane ride would be worth a try. Boy was it ever! I felt the plane was superior to the helicopter in that we had more time to look at the individual sights, but it was Bruce and his knowledge, wit, and care for his clients that made the trip a true experience.

I got to sit in the co-pilot's seat and go over the pre-flight check off list. As an engineer, that was really cool and Bruce explained some of the controls that I didn't fully understand.

It's the little touches that make Wings Over Kauai so exceptional. My wife received a shell lei and a flower from Bruce's home garden upon arrival. At the conclusion of the trip a CD of Kauai was waiting for us and it had a picture of the two of us on the CD cover.

If you are looking for an attraction in Kauai that will leave you very pleased, visit Bruce and company at Wings Over Kauai.

Review Title: Wonderful flight with a top notch company
Review Text:
Ellen and Bruce, the owners of Wings over Kauai are two of the nicest people that you’ll ever meet. The reservation process with Ellen was smooth and enjoyable and she is very personable.

We had received a phone call from Ellen yesterday letting us know that they had an unexpected inspection of their larger plane (GA-8 Airvan) scheduled for today so we wouldn’t all be able to fly together on our scheduled sightseeing flight. She had offered us the option to take two separate flights on their smaller aircraft (Cessna 172) or to take their competitor Air Venture (she had even talked to Air Venture about available flight times with them). We decided to stick with Wings over Kauai and were glad we did.

We decided that my step son and I would take the first flight at 11 am and that my wife and step daughter would take the later flight at 12:30 pm. Ellen picked us up at the ABC store near the ship (it’s about a 10 minute walk or a free shuttle ride) and we headed to the airport where we weighed in and waited until Bruce was ready. I sat up front with Bruce and my step son sat in the back. The Cessna was definitely small and was by far the smallest aircraft that I’ve ever been in, and I was a bit nervous at first. Bruce’s calm manner and professionalism quickly put me at ease though. We both had on headphones so we could hear Bruce’s narration and converse with him. As we taxied out, he had me read off his preflight check list which was fun. He is very methodical and safety conscious so I felt like we were in very good hands. Soon we were cleared for takeoff and it didn’t take long for us to be airborne. We flew over Waimea Canyon, the Na Pali coast, the waterfall from Fantasy Island, and even saw the summit of Mount Waialeale which Bruce said was rare (it’s one of the rainiest spots on earth with an average of 426 inches of rain per year). We saw numerous mountains, waterfalls, beaches, and beautiful coastline on our flight and Bruce is a veritable encyclopedia of knowledge. I haven’t done any helicopter flights but couldn’t imagine it being any better than this, and at a much cheaper price than a helicopter too. We flew over the Pride of America on our way back to the airport and all too soon were coming in for a smooth, smooth landing.

My wife and step daughter were waiting at the airport for their flight so Ellen took a picture of all four of us in front of the plane. That picture ended up on the cover of the free dvd that they gave us (which features footage from what we saw on the flight but not from our specific flight). Ellen drove us back to the ABC store (she offered to take us to the ship but we wanted to buy a few t-shirts) and bid us a fond farewell. Later, when my wife returned, her and my step daughter raved about their flight and we all compared notes. What a wonderful experience.
