Review Text:
This is not just a review of the Wings Over Kauai marvelous circle island flight, but also about the aloha of their family, Bruce, Ellen and daughter Mary.

Reservations were easy, happy and fun, when I talked with Ellen, to reserve two seats for us. We talked story, and just had a ball. Ellen is so full of life and aloha, and infectious happy laughter makes a person feel like you are talking to a long time friend.

On the day we were sheduled, Ellen calls and reminds us of the flight, and says everything is a " go". She also says that she will not be there, but her daughter Mary will be running the office.

Kidding around, I say " Well , just how am I going to give you an aloha hug ? " Ellen replys " Give the hug to my daughter, and she can pass it on ! " How cool is that. I love this island and the people.

We are excited about flying in their brand new G-8 Aerovan. That puppy has room for 6, but generally they just fly four. Huge windows for photo opportunities, and plenty of leg room. Seats run along each side seperated by an isle in the center.

Each passenger has a headseat and mic, and Bruce , the owner, and pilot, visits and talks with each individual, calling them by their first names. The naration of the flight is excellent, as Bruce has years and years of experience flying the tour in his Cessna 172, plus he has many, many years as a resident on Kauai. Knows his stuff.

Prior to departure we weigh in and sign in....Mary escorts us out to the G-8, to the ladder leading into the main cabin. She will take pre boarding photos with your camera , as well as hers.

Also the ladies all receive a kukui nut lei...which I placed over Erica's shoulders and gave her the traditional kiss. The fun had already begun and we were still on the ground.

Take off was smooth, and I rode up in the right seat, ( co-pilot seat ) next to Bruce. Not sure if it makes any difference, but I was a professional pilot for nearly 40 years. No stick time in the G-8, but it was great fun helping read off the check list, and feeling a bit like part of the aircrew.

Take off was smooth and we gently banked to the right, and began our climb out for the Circle Island Tour. The passengers in the back had their cameras ready.

Bruce flys slow and at an altitude that is superb for photos as we were treated to marvelous panoramic views of the garden island. Seems like we fly about the same routes as the helo companies, with thoughtful attention to noise abatement in certain areas.

Roughly, we cruised past Kalapaki Beach, and Nawiliwili Harbor. On our right the cameras clicked with shots of Kipu Kai, Maha'ulepu, The Hyatt and Poipu. Turning inland we crossed over the coffee fields of Kalaheo, and then to some of the canyons in the Hanapepe Valley.

Wonderful vistas of Waimea Canyon opened up, and then flew over the ridge and waimea canyon road, and the deep valleys that lead to the Napali Coast. Soon we were cruising along the Napali Coast . Banking inland about Hanalei, the interior beauty, lush valleys, water falls and rivers were marvelous. More natural tresures passed beneath us, as we circled Wialua Falls.....

That is just part of the flying experience, you will be seeing much more, and even though we live on Kauai, learned all kinds of new information about the island.

Flight time is nearly up, and we fly very near our condo, at Banyon Harbor, which is on the approach to runway 3.

We have a cross wind, and Bruce landed so sofly that I could not feel the wheel touch down. Maybe jus a slight kiss as he rolled it on. I kidded him " You had better call the tower and confirm that we are on the ground ! " Bruce just smiled.

Now remember when Mary took photos of both couples prior to departure. Well, we taxi up to the Commuter Terminal and shut down. Mary brings out the steps for easy exiting of the aircraft.

Everyone is happy and smiling, Mary presents us with WOK's professional DVD of the route of flight. Back ground music is by IZ. And, on the front of the DVD plastic holder is the picture of each individual couple. Yep, Erica and I are pictured just below the WINGS OVER KAUAI name on the top.

Will just finish by saying that the G-8, is a product of Australia, and flown as a tour aircraft down under. It can haul the weight. Which, is great for those who weigh more than the max limit to fly a helo tour without purchasing an extra seat, or a percentage of an extra seat.

No extra charge. There is plenty of leg and shoulder room, and I belive the cost is about $ 249.00 for two people. That is pretty reasonable and about half the cost of some of the helo tours give or take a few bucks. Not bad !

We looked out our DVD this morning, now this is professionally done. It is not a dvd of our particular flight, and is outstanding. Perfect for showing friends and family upon returning to your home base. And it is also included. No extra charge.

The Wings Over Kauai cirdle island tour, was most outstanding. Bruce, Ellen and Mary were wonderful, and make each individual passenger feel like they are the only people that exist on the planet. Lots of individual customer service and aloha.

Denny and Erica
Lihue, Hawaii

Review Title: Why would you want to take a helicopter???
Review Text:
It appears that the key choice in chosing an air tour is to go by helicopter or by airplane. The hotels always seem to recommend the helicopter tour, but why? Could it be that they just recommend the most expensive option? Take the airplane! It's half the cost, and you see the same places.

Captain Bruce of Wings of Kauai has been flying for years, and his skill sets proved it to me. As a commercial pilot myself, I notice things that most people don't. I VALUE SAFETY ABOVE ALL ELSE. Case in point. There was another aircraft within sight that decided to fly up a canyon, one where the clouds were very low. As I sat in the seat, I wondered if our captain was going to follow him. My concern was that the clouds were too low to remain legally VFR (visual flight reference), a standard that tour planes must adhere to for safety sake because no IFR (Instrument Flight Rules) plan had been filed. Flying into or too close to those clouds can spell trouble, after all, where are the sides of the canyon if you can't see them? Draw your own conclusions.

Captain Bruce made a consciencous decision to take a different route, and we saw the same sights. Later I asked him why he took that route, and he replied, "Safety comes first, and I did not want to risk my passengers". There is a saying in aviation: There are old pilots and there are bold pilots, but there are no old, bold pilots. I appreciated his decision and concern for safety rather than take a risk just we could see the same sight from a different perspective.

There are two rows of seats in the aircraft. He only books the seats on the right hand side of the aircraft so everyone gets a window seat. Great for visuals and great for photos. Would you get that treatment in a crowded helicopter?

We actually flew through a double rainbow that totally engulfed the aircraft. I've never seen anything like it. I totally encircled the aircraft. It was above us, beside us and below us. I've never experienced anything like it before.

In any case, I give Wings over Kauai a five star rating. Great people. Great trip. Great memories. Great photos.

Review Text:
We decided to take this flight whilst calling at the island on a Princess Cruises tour of the Hawaian Islands. Whilst considering our shore excursions before leaving England we knew that we wanted to see Kauai from the air, but should we choose a Helicopter or a Plane? Princess wanted US$269 each for a 55 minute shared helicopter flight including ground transport; WoK charged us US$249 FOR THE TWO OF US including 'trimmings' (see below) with exclusive use of the plane and ground transport. They also confirmed that if, for some reason, the ship could not dock we would not be charged. Always one for a bargain, I booked - but was it any good?

It was arranged that Ellen would meet us at a shopping centre close to the ship at 10.30am for our 11.00am flight for a private car transfer to the airport - but she was late!! I have never known anyone so apologetic about being 3 minutes late (try waiting for a local train in the UK Ellen, they don't even call it late in their performance statistics unless it is 5 minutes late and they don't even apologise if it is 13 minutes late).

After our transfer to the airport during which Ellen told us all about Bruce and her backgrounds we carried out the paperwork (and weighing!) with Ellen whilst Bruce prepared the plane. My wife was presented with a flower for her hair and a nut lei to wear and we proceeded to the plane, having our photo taken alongside it.

My wife, having a slightly more petite build than me (!), was chosen as being the best person for the front seat with me having room to spread out in the back. She helped Bruce with his pre-flight checks and we were then away. The in-flight refreshments were not used by us - we were too interested in the scenery.

We had been warned to wear a dark top (to prevent reflections in the windows) and as a result of this I did not need to open windows to take my numerous photographs.

Was it a good decision to take a plane rather than a helicopter? As the saying goes 'you pays your money, you takes your choice'. Of necessity, the place operates at a higher level than the helicopter and cannot go deep into the valleys; however, for a lot of our flight I could see a helicopter operating beneath us. It appeared very close to the ground and I cannot believe that it could have provided as good a photo as some of those taken by me on my rather basic camera. Ours was also very much a personalised trip whereas a helicopter would have been shared, following a pre-determined route.

We were able to fly over our ship to take pictures from the air and also more unusual sights such as the massive Costco and Car Park from the air.

As we returned to the airport it was an interesting experience to land on one runway at the same time as a 'proper' passenger plane was landing on the main runway. Like others, we were presented with a DVD with our own pictures on the front.

We were intending going on afterwards to the Kilohana Plantation which we thought was close-by but was actually a fair distance away. Ellen offered to take us as she was heading in that direction. She needn't have done this, however, it was typical of Ellen and Bruce. Their main concern was to ensure that we had a great day, which we did.

If you book with WoK you will not be sorry. Enjoy the experience; we certainly did.

Review Text:
I'd been hoping to rent a single engine airplane during our recent trip to Kauai. I'm a private pilot, and my wonderful wife was looking for a way to see the island while allowing me to indulge my flying passion. We found Ellen and Captain Bruce searching on line, and are glad we did. I logged the flight time as "pilot in command" with Bruce in the co-pilot seat, and my wife-family photographer in the back seat.

Bruce and Ellen's late model Cessna 172S is spacious and clean. What I appreciated most was how stable the aircraft flys around the beautiful mountain palis. And with it's high wing configuration, you get to see everything around and below you. My wife took over 100 photos during our 70 minute adventure.

After circling the island and flying over Wiama Canyon, we contacted the Lihue tower for a clearance to land. The entire experience was excellent, providing an up close view of areas otherwise inaccessible. As a private pilot, it was a real thrill for me to land the aircraft on the same island runway that the large commercial jets, including the one we had flown in used. Whether you're a pilot, or you let Captain Bruce do all the flying for you, I'd recommend Wings Over Hawaii...for anyone wanting a safe, slow ride around the Garden Isle!

Review Title: Great day. Great weather. Great pictures. Great people.  So ... DO IT!
Review Text:
This was our third trip to Hawaii, and second to Kauai. Last time here we took the helicopter tour & thought it was great. This time we decided to fly again, but wanted a better opportunity for photography. We reviewed all the brochures, but Wings Over Kauai was the only one that offered open-window capabilities. We're also very environmentally sensitive about any place we go (yes, we pick up other people's trash), and liked the idea that the plane used so much less fuel than a chopper. That settled it! Pilot Bruce and his wife Ellen welcomed us warmly with a Plumeria flower for my hair and a Kukui nut lei. There was a cooler in the back with water and soda at no charge. My husband is the photographer in the family, so I opted for the back seat, although photo ops from that viewpoint were also possible through the open window. The Bose noise-cancelling headphones were fantastic, and we were able to talk to the pilot while in flight, asking questions all along the way. Bruce is so knowledgeable about the landscapes we were viewing, offering history, geography, geology, and agricultural tidbits that were both educational and entertaining. There was no problem with him turning the plane for certain photos, and we were lucky enough to get shots of Mt. Waialeale when it was not covered in clouds. At 5,148 feet, this mountain is the wettest spot on the planet, averaging rainfall of 460 inches per year. Waimea Canyon and the NaPali Coast were indescribably beautiful from a bird's-eye view. Because the plane held only 4 persons (including pilot), my husband and I felt like it was our own private tour. It's windy and chilly, though, in the back seat once that window is opened, so be prepared by bringing a scarf for your head and a sweatshirt or jacket (we flew in December). The cost was very reasonable for the one-hour flight ~ and if we have one suggestion, it's that Bruce and Ellen should offer a longer tour. Before we took off, Ellen took our picture by the plane and surprised us when we landed with with a video disc with us on the cover. The video was produced by their son, Carter. So it's truly a family business, and we were happy to support such a venture
.
Great day. Great weather. Great pictures. Great people. So ... DO IT! You won't be disappointed!

We signed our life away, stepped on the scale - really a formality. Bruce arrived with the last couple he took up, and they were beaming. Tor got us into the plane. Probably due to decades as a pilot, Bruce's natural confidence set us at ease right away. He told us what to expect as far as the way the plane moves ahead of time.

It was neat feeling like part of the flight crew. We were able to listen in on the chatter with the tower. And although I did not expect it, both my husband and I felt afterward that there was something really special about taking our tour in an airplane. It's an extra feeling to the tour that is hard to explain, but you will understand it once you go up. Most of our pictures have a bit of the window or the wing in there. And for us, that is just so perfect. We have a remembrance of the phenomenal beauty of Kauai and a reminder of that incredible nostalgic and peaceful feeling of slowly flying over pristine beauty.

Bruce was great at pointing things out - an interactive tour. Really more like a personal conversation between Bruce who knows the Island, it's history, it's ecology and people - and the people lucky enough to get a seat on his plane. We just can't say enough about that - this is a personal tour. Not a prepackaged production. This is one of the few things I'd gladly spend money on again if we are lucky enough to see Hawaii again.

Review Title: Once In A Lifetime Experience... Unbelievable!
Review Text:
My wife and I had the trip of a lifetime with Wings Over Kaua'i on our recent trip to the island. We went to three different islands over the span of 12 days and saw many different things, however, this was the unquestionable highlight of our trip.

The company is a true family affair with Bruce, Ellen and their children, and they made us immediately feel welcome and a part of their extended family.

Bruce is an exceptional pilot and perhaps an even better tour guide. His knowledge of the island -- traditions, culture, geography, etc. -- is made even better by his knowledge of the climate and agriculture that you see during the flight.

We boarded his plane at the Lihu'e airport and took off on a route that followed the Eastern Coast south. We then turned West near Poi'pu and saw many things along the shore. During that part, and the entire trip, Bruce mixed in good conversation with fun facts and information about the island. It was as much of a learning experience as it was a sightseeing tour for us.

He then turned the plane northwest so that we could see the views of Waimea Canyon and eventually the dramatic Napili Coast. Words and photos do not do justice when describing these areas. It is truly an awesome sight and something that is hard to fathom. However, seeing it from the air adds an incredible dimension that you can't tell from land.

Bruce then took us along the Northern Coast of the island and inland to see Wailua Falls and other waterfalls. Again, an awe-inspiring experience.

When we booked the flight, Ellen warned us that the day we were going up could be a bit bumpy because of the tradewinds, but other than a few minor air pockets, it did not bother us at all. The entire flight was very comfortable for both of us.

Bruce also gave us the opportunity to open the window and take photos through that. We were amazed at the photo quality with the window both open and closed.

Overall, you cannot go wrong with booking this flight. It is unquestionable one of the best things I have experienced in our life. The price was very reasonable, and the quality of the experience was second-to-none.

Review Title: The Best Way  to See Kauai
Review Text:
When you get to Kauai you will see all sorts of ads for helicopter rides. I'm sure they're nice, but they are expensive. Wings over Kauai is a ride in a small airplane for about half the price, and it is great, personalized tour for you and your family. The tour takes about 70 minutes. Be sure to bring your camera. (The operator e-mail souvenir pictures and video of your family.)

The owner operator gives you a wonderful guided tour of what may be the most beautiful place in the world. There are scores of waterfalls; misty mountains, green, green valleys; remote, multi-blue beaches; surf and sand; in all a tropical mountain paradise. There is no way you can see all of of Kauai without taking flight, and there is no better way to fly than in a small plane.

Helicoptors rides are cool in themselves, but for this you don't need the distraction of a thrill ride. The plane is simple, smooth and prefect for Kauai. Wings Over Kauai is a family buisness where you will ride with the owner, Bruce, meet his wife, and maybe even one of their kids. It's a warm safe feeling. Bruce is a easy going, knowlegable guide with a gentle sense of humor. He will show and tell everything about Kauai, where the movies were filmed, where the stars live, how agriculture works; he may even tell you the down side of the cost of living or the public schools. And he will show you the tail of Puff the Magic Dragon in the town called Hanelei. I highly recommend Wings Over Kauai.

Review Title: Hate Flying & Heights, But Loved This!
Review Text:
I detest flying and heights, am a "safety nut", and add to all that, I'm cheap, which is why I was so reluctant to book an aerial tour of Kauai. However, I just had to get my eyes on the aerial views I kept seeing pictures of so I took the plunge with Wings Over Kauai. Reasons I chose them over a helicopter ride (and why it was the right choice!):
1. Cheaper---this tour is literally half the cost of a copter ride. The value is unbelievable.
2. Personal---we would have been on the copter with 4 other people plus the pilot. This tour is limited to 3 persons plus Bruce, the pilot, so my husband and I were able to go it alone and have a very tailored, personal experience. Bruce was so knowledgeable about the island and sites he pointed out. We asked lots of questions, and had a wonderful, personal experience.
3. Safety---I kept reading about recent helicopter crashes on aerial tours. WOK has a perfect safety record. I was shocked at how comfortable Bruce made me feel on the fight. I felt completely safe.
4. Stability---the small plane provides a more stable riding experience, and I am really susceptible to motion sickness. Bruce helped me with some "tricks", and I didn't feel badly or get sick the entire flight. I was truly amazed by this.

If you are considering an aerial tour of Kauai (and you should---the views did not disappoint), you should choose WOK. Bruce and Ellen are kind, helpful, considerate, and extremely accommodating.

Thanks a million, Bruce and Ellen!

Review Text:
Please, please do yourself a favor and book a ride with Captain Bruce on Wings Over Kauai Tours! My new husband and I were recently in Kauai for our honeymoon and we knew that we wanted to see Kauai by air. My husband tends to get seasick/airsick/carsick, so I knew I wanted a quiet, uncrowded experience for him. We called on a Tuesday morning to inquire about possible reservations and were able to fly that afternoon!

Here are the POSITIVES:
(1) You get to meet Captain Bruce's wife, Ellen, at the private terminal and learn all about the family (even the kids!). Ladies are presented with a special lei and a flower (which smelled so delicious, I spent the rest of the week trying to track down in perfume form only to find out nobody makes it!). We laughed when he offered us "in flight" service before our flight by giving us each a mint and collecting our wrappers! (They also provide drinks.) My husband got to sit in front with Bruce and do the pre-flight checklist, which made us both feel like we understood the plane better and was really interesting!
(3) You are the only ones on your flight! We were so glad we booked with WOKT after we saw all the noisy helicopters buzz in and out across the way from the private plane terminal, dropping off and picking up hoards of people. Also, other small planes had numerous people on them. On the WOKT plane, only three passengers are allowed at a time, so everyone has a window seat and everyone knows each other.
(4) The flight is not noisy and you get to talk to the pilot whenever you want. There was nice background music in our ear sets, but we were more interested in talking to Bruce about the island.

We found the WOKT pricing to be extremely reasonable and affordable, especially compared with our experience before with helicopters and other small plane tours. Because Bruce took time to get to know us before and during our flight, he made sure to point out or spend extra time on sights that would be of interest to us. Negatives? Absolutely none! We talked about our flight the rest of the week and the photos we took were the best of our trip. After we got home, there was a nice email for us from Ellen with a photo they took of us before our flight, a great reminder of an awesome time! Thanks Bruce and Ellen!

We took the Pali Mist tour with WOK today (Friday). Making the reservation was very easy. I was about to confirm my reservation on a helicopter tour when I came across the reviews on tripadvisor about Wings over Kauai. It has a 5 star rating with not a single negative or mediocre review so i though it had to be GREAT!

We called and booked the same day and it turned out to be the highlight of my trip to Hawaii so much so that i am still thinking about it and want to write my first review ever on Tripadvisor about it.

I wont go into details about my trip since a lot of travelleres have already written a lot of accurate stuff but I will say that you will definitely miss out on something if you donot take this tour. It is indeed the best $100/person you will ever spend on Hawaii. Without giving details on the trip, spend that money and experience a flight of a lifetime.

Review Text:
My wife and I, along with our 10-yr. old daughter Alana, took this wonderful tour on June 13th. The whole family at Wings Over Kauai was great - including Bruce and Ellen's daughter who checked us in. The personal touch was really great and we recommend this tour to everyone! Our flight was 70 minutes long and Bruce's commentary was thorough and never boring. Of course, the tour is also much cheaper than the helicopter offered on the island. The plane is perfect for taking pictures and the noise-canceling headsets with Hawaiian music in the background is a nice touch. Most of all, of course, Kauai is breathtaking from the air. The island had just experienced some heavy rainfall and we must have seen 100 waterfalls that day. The highlight of the tour is the Napali coast and we flew over Napali for quite some time. What a place! After the trip with Bruce, we would never take a tour with anyone else. Bruce really involves you with the tour and the plane was comfortable and perfect for the 3 of us. Use Wings Over Kauai to get acquainted with Kauai - you won't regret it.
Rick from Ohio

Review Title: Totally wonderful .. no need to splurge on a heli tour ...
Review Text: Very nice little family run outfit ... Ellen and Bruce are extremely pleasant in every way ... Ellen was very helpful on the phone and in person even for travel tips around Kauai .. The price of the ride is so much more affordable than a helicopter tour .. And I cannot imagine that it can be all that better to be worth double the price ... Kauai is Kauai from the air .. It is still just as incredibly beautiful ... Bruce was wonderful as a pilot ... It was a very enjoyable experience and he makes it a very personal one by teaching you a bit about flying too .. They were also very accomodating to our special situation of having a 2.5 year old with us ... My Mom and I flew on one flight and my husband by himself on another flight ... Ellen even called us and had us reschedule when they were a little doubtful about the weather ... instead of just letting us go in the okay weather and let us deal with it .. I thought that that was very professional and very nice of them ... The flight itself was very comfortable ... Overall Highly recommended ...

Review Title: Wonderful Welcome to the Garden Isle
Review Text:
I booked Wings Over Kauai after reading several positive reviews and wanting something my entire family, including our infant, could enjoy. I knew I wanted an aerial tour of Kauai, but was as leery of the helicopter tours as they were of my little one. Because we were planning on flying with an infant, I wanted to make sure we wouldn't disturb or ruin anyone else's flight, so I was looking for a tour that was smaller, more personal and unique. With Wings Over Kauai, we got that and more!
When I called to reserve the tour, I spoke with Ellen who was both knowledgeable and VERY friendly. She answered all my questions and was more than willing to work to help accommodate our little one. The plane they fly is a 4-seater, so there wouldn't be anyone else to disturb, and she asked if there was anyplace specific we were looking to fly over so that they could try to work that into the flight plan.
The day of the tour, we showed up early and both Ellen and Bruce (the pilot) greeted us and even presented a gift to our little 'keiki'. When it came time to check-in and go over all of the preflight information, Ellen was helpful and made sure to answer all of our questions and concerns. They even offered us a car seat so that my husband wouldn't have to hold our little one the whole flight, as well as small ear plugs to help with the noise. They also offer a children's-sized headset, but we figured 10 months was a little young to enjoy or even keep it on.
From take-off until landing, the flight was amazing! Bruce was both professional and personable. He explained all of the piloting jargon and information that was passing over the radio, and he also provided a narrative that gave information and details about what we were currently flying over. He did his best to allow me ample opportunity to take photos and also informed me of potential photo ops that would be coming up. Our little one had such a good time that she spent most of the flight laughing, cooing and just enjoying the air from the car seat. My husband enjoyed himself and had a great view even from the rear seat.
One warning for those not used to flying in small aircraft: even on a clear day, it can get a bit bumpy and the nature of the island (mountains and valleys) make for some air pockets. By the end of the flight, my stomach was definitely feeling a bit rough. It had nothing to do with the plane or how it was being piloted, but it is something to keep in mind for those who might not have stomachs of steel. Bruce was very helpful and prepared for any problems - he carried the obligatory air sickness bags but also had ginger candy, water, and a cold cloth that came in VERY handy as we got ready to land.

Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend Wings Over Kauai. Bruce and Ellen were very friendly and the ride itself worth EVERY penny. For both my husband and myself, it was almost half the cost of a helicopter tour, and being able to bring our little one and fly a personal tour made it an even greater value. Anyone looking for a fun and unique way to tour Kauai should definitely consider flying on Wings Over Kauai!

Review Title: To Ride a Helicopter in Kauai or Not
Review Text:
Definitely not! I took a tour with Wings Over Kauai and my experience was fantastic. I chose Wings Over Kauai because I felt like I was chartering my own private plane. Wings Over Kauai has a four-seater airplane, so it will only be Captain Bruce and your party (2-3 people). Wings Over Kauai also has the option to customize your tour to allow you to fly over the sites you want to see. I wanted to see all the waterfalls on Kauai and Captain Bruce, the friendliest Captain you will ever fly with, flew us around the entire island and took us, as he jokingly told his wife afterwards, "to every [--] waterfall on the island". If you think that helicopters have a better view than an airplane, think again. The airplane Wings Over Kauai uses is engulfed with windows and I never noticed the wings my entire flight. I guaranteed that a flight with Wings Over Kauai will be a highlight of your trip!

If cost is a concern, it shouldn't be. You should visit an Activity World booth, one is conveniently located at Coconut Coast Market. You will need to attend a timeshare presentation. Timeshare presentations are incredibly lame, but well worth your time. My tour should have been $260, 70 min. for two people, but it was drastically reduced to $96.

Review Text:

Review Title: FANTASTIC!!! Why take a helicopter when you can take Wings Over Kauai?!
Review Text:
WINGS OVER KAUAI: A 70-minute flight around the entire island in a 3-passenger Cessna plane. Owner-operated by Bruce & Ellen Coulombe, this was a wonderful alternative to viewing Kauai from above without being in a helicopter.

We chose Wings Over Kauai because Bruce came highly recommended on numerous trip web sites – and Bruce has a lot of experience – not just flying in general, but specifically flying over Kauai (that was important to us). There was another plane outfit that had 2 pilots – one with a lot of experience flying over Kauai, the other with only about 2 years – and we could not get a guarantee of getting the one with the more experience.

We were so happy we went with Wings Over Kauai!!! Bruce was very professional and we couldn’t have felt safer… he’s a very intelligent & contientious pilot, to be sure!! The plane is a 3-passenger Cessna – which gives everyone a window – and creates for a very tailor-made, personal flight experience!

Another wonderful aspect of going with Wings Over Kauai is the fact that it was about half the price of a helicopter tour, yet just as spectacular…. And I have the photos to prove it!

Review Title: Excellant way to end Anniversary in the Islands!
Review Text: My husband decided at the last minute to book a flight over Kaui while we were in Kona.  THe Blue Shak on Kona booked it for us 2 days before we arrived.  The weather was so clear and even it wasn't raining on the wettest place on earth.  Ellen and Bruce are down to earth folks that truly want to ensure you have the best experience every.  Bruce is an experienced with the plants and fomation of the island.  I felt MUCH safer with his plane that the small helicoptors that kept going in and out of the mountains.  We were able to take a nice photo and I have some clear photos of Mt. Walielie and the water falls and coastlines.  I felt the price was very reasonable for a 70 minute flight.  Please think about using Wings over Kaui for a truly unique experience.  Make sure you battery is charged on your camera and you have PLENTY of space on your memory card if you have a digital camera.. You are going to need it.

Review Title: skip the helicopters: take a Wings Over Kauai flight!
Review Text: We wanted to see Kauai from the air without the rapid motion, daredevil atmosphere, and vertiginous flying patterns used by the many helicopter tour companies. Our innkeeper recommended Bruce and Ellen Coulombe's Wings Over Kauai. Bruce, a very experienced pilot, flies up to three passengers at a time in a small fixed-wing plane. Every attention is paid to safety and comfort. I don't like enclosed spaces and was a bit nervous about the size of the plane, but Bruce's professional and friendly demeanor quickly had me at ease. He is a wonderful narrator as well and the noise-excluding Bose headphones and mics let us speak normally and enjoy his extensive commentary. Ellen runs the reservation desk at the Lihue airport commuter terminal. The Coulombes are delightful, warm, and welcoming people. We were accommodated the same day we called, and had a fantastic flight. Photography was easy and convenient, with great results! We signed up for the 70-minute flight and saw the entire island, including the crater of Mt. Wai'ale'ale, the Na Pali coast, and also the northeastern area, which most aerial tours skip. I highly recommend Wings over Kauai for an enjoyable, safe, and fascinating experience!

Review Title: The only way to really see the island in 70 minutes
Review Text: If you are planning this in your itinerary, note the tour is based at the Lihue (LIH) airport general aviation facilites.  The 70 minute flight ties for the best memory we have of our five days in Kauai (with a catamaran tour of the Na Pali coast).  Two years ago we took a helicopter tour of Maui, and we just feel more comfortable in flying something with wings on it, plus the cost is about one-half of an equally long helicopter flight and covers more of the island.  Bruce, the owner-operator and chief pilot has a prior professional agronomy background (on Kauai).  He was very knowledgeable during his interesting narration of ground features.
